reviews.author: Jacqueline K.
reviews.text: We had a nice - and perhaps thankfully short - stay at Kalaloch Campground. The campground has nice facilities (clean bathrooms and even warm water running out of the taps). However, it is not a place to stay at if one were looking for peace and did not get one of the spots further from the road. I booked D002 aware of the potential of "traffic noise." But I underestimated the magnitude of traffic and noise. Site D002 is right next to day parking. I could see cars pointed right at the site and people walking by. That issue mainly went away at night. Traffic noise of cars were tolerable. What was alarming - and unexpected - was the noise of giant flat bed trucks carrying tons of logged trees speeding down the road. They start early - we heard them by sunrise. In short, Kalaloch is not the campground for you if you are seeking quiet and peace and the only sites available are along the 101.

reviews.author: Rylee W.
reviews.text: Beautiful camp spot! Very large area in the back for a tent, and the parking spot was very large. You can see the neighbors to the left, so keep that in mind. Picnic table was very close to the parking spot, and the site itself was very spacious!

reviews.author: Rylee W.
reviews.text: Beautiful campground! You are very close to the neighbors to the left, but there is a small pond to the right so it is very private that way. Camp fire ring and table were very nice and clean. The parking spot to this space does dip down a little when you pull in, but other than that is is pretty level.

reviews.author: claudia m.
reviews.text: Beautiful Beaches. Nice campground, clean restrooms. No shower.  No cell service.  No clear sky for starlink.

reviews.author: Joel R.
reviews.text: Visting Kalaloch on the Washington State Olympic Peninsula is always a great experience.  The Park Service team maintaining the facilities are doing a great job.

reviews.author: Adam B.
reviews.text: It’s hard to beat a camp ground like this. Right next to the ocean, quiet, reasonably clean bathrooms. If you are itching for a meal, Kalaloch Lodge is 1/4 mile down the street and has great food plus a small convenience store. It would be great if the campground had showers, but we used the Forks Swim Club and Gym day pass option for a quick clean up. Our couple of days here was great (spot E010 - and if you reserve this spot be sure to walk through the bush trail at the back of the site for a private view of the beach!)

reviews.author: Anthony R.
reviews.text: One of my favorite places. Hard to get reservations, but if you are flexible and time it right Kalaloch is a place most would enjoy. I like the variety of what each beach along the way from Beach 1 to Ruby Beach has to offer.

reviews.author: Michelle P.
reviews.text: Love this campground, we have been multiple times and I highly recommend staying here. The staff has always been nice and helpful. It is maintained well. We stayed in C10 this time and the only improvement I would suggest is keeping the fire pits updated/maintained. Ours was rusty and broken. The metal circle was broken very badly and sharp. Other than that - we had an amazing time!

reviews.author: Jennifer V.
reviews.text: Restrooms were adequately clean. It was very unclear where to access clean water for tent campers. As far as we could tell, the intent was for us to use the hose provided at the dump station for RVs. However, it would be very helpful to have this marked since it is unusual for a campground, and not familiar to those who don't use RVs.

reviews.author: Gary C.
reviews.text: The grounds are beautiful with majestic trees and great beaches.

reviews.author: Hadassah C.
reviews.text: The campsite and campground was beautiful and clean. The bathrooms were disgusting.

reviews.author: Michael S.
reviews.text: First time camping at Kalaloch. Definitely won't be the last. I think I picked the best campsite there. It was bigger than any other I saw. It was close enough to the beach that wind wasn't a factor. The weather was amazing so I lucked out all around.

reviews.author: Sandy A.
reviews.text: Absolutely wonderful campground. Tremendous views, clean and well run. I highly recommend!

reviews.author: Nathan F.
reviews.text: Great campsite. Extremely close to the beach. The only thing that would make this better is if the water was working at the bathroom and if they had hand soap. Other than that it was excellent.

reviews.author: Mya A.
reviews.text: Such a beautiful campground! We caught one of the best sunsets ever on the beach and enjoyed a peaceful, relaxing evening. Bathroom facilities are decent, camp spots are pretty small and close together, but decently private with lots of foliage around

reviews.author: Dawn J.
reviews.text: Great site. Very little noise. Bathrooms could be a little cleaner. Great hosts.

reviews.author: Shannon K.

Roadway noise noise was loud but not that often, so it wasn't a bother. It was nice to hear the waves at night! Nice to be so close to the beach, and there weren't a ton of outside visitors, so it felt like you had the beach all to yourself. Was an awesome place to stay.

reviews.author: Shawna H.
reviews.text:
Kalaloch is so beautiful and one of the most amazing places on the Peninsula to stay and visit. The trash left behind on the beaches and in the restrooms are absolutely horrible and people need to do better.  We picked up over 20 lbs of trash from the beach, a tire and litter scattered throughout the park over the weekend, it was ridiculous. And just because the NPS has employees and rangers cleaning restrooms, doesn't mean they should have to clean up all of your trash, litter and bags of garbage. If you want these treasured places to be available in the future, take care of them. 
Our site this time was just above the Tree of Life and we spent more time than necessary guiding traffic for people searching for the Tree of Life, assuming based on Google, that it was in the campground.. its not. Access is from the public parking lot and via trail down to the beach. It would be amazing if there was some signage that it is not accessible from the campground in order to avoid being disturbed constantly while enjoying such an amazing place with your family. 
We love Kalaloch and being Peninsula locals, will stay every chance we can...if I could give any tips for camping: Be prepared for wind, some very cold nights, even when its warm...  and for the love, leave it the way you found it and pick up your trash. Also, stay off the already debilitating structure of the tree. Take photos, admire, be in aww of the beauty...but leave the tree alone and stop climbing all over it.  
Enjoy the amazing beauty because it really is a beautiful place.

reviews.text: I would like to see trails in the forest linking the beaches if it could be done with minimal impact to the ecosystem. But doing that with those ocean views was no problem at all. The RV dumping station was also very nice.

Short walk to the bathrooms. Some sites at 2 bars of cell service for tmoblie but this site is not one of them. Beautiful site tho

reviews.text: We had a lovely time at this camp ground. Our spot was nice and clean and the factor adequate. Loop A bathroom was out of order but it was fixed pretty quickly. Location not too far from Hoh Rainforest Trailhead, Ruby Beach or Forks, WA.

reviews.author: Alice R.
reviews.text:
The campground itself is beautiful. We had a "low privacy" site but really it didn't seem that bad for the first 2 nights we were there. There are so many cool trees that swallow the campground that it really helps immerse you. The beach was extremely accessible and you could easily walk down it to get up to the Kalaloch Lodge if you didn't want to go by road (you will have to get your feet wet, just so you know). Not the best campsite for wanting to explore other parts of Olympic National Park as you have to drive around an hour to get ANYWHERE from your campsite (even the nearest town). 

On one of our last nights we walked several miles down the beach to where there were rocks. I want to say the furthest we made it was a bit past Beach 3. It was so unbelievably fun to climb on the rocks while the tide was slowly coming in and we even saw a bald eagle who had caught a SEA OTTER and was eating it. An unbelievable experience, truly. 

The only downside to our stay was that on our final day we were woken up by other camp visitors walking THROUGH our campsite. Like, right between our tent and our campfire- not even trying to avoid it. They did this multiple times with their entire family despite me verbally yelling at them to please not. They even dropped trash on our campsite (unintentionally, most likely). I was so frustrated with them that I went to the booth to talk to a ranger and that was the one day there were no booth hours. I got back to my campsite and tried to call the help line or just SOMEONE to come handle it because it made me extremely angry that they wouldn't listen and thought out campsite was just a path for them instead of going around like we did. Of course, as soon as I dialed the number, they hopped in their RV and left.

reviews.text: Lovely beach, campground is ok, but like many national parks, forests etc, in need of some upkeep.  I also noticed the large number of vacant campsites despite the campground always being 100% reserved.  This is due to many things, such as the refund policy, I mean if you are not going to refund me for my reservation then why should anyone cancel it.  Also, I made my reservation two weeks in advance, something came up and I wanted to change my 7 days reservation to 5 days.  I was not able to due to rules in the reservation system that did not allow changes for 14 days after making your reservations, essentially meaning that my reservation could not be modified or canceled.  So, my campsite sat empty for two nights when someone else could have been there.

reviews.text: The Kalaloch area is blessed with great natural beauty, and there's plenty to see from the campground and other spots in the area. I found the campground cleaner than most, including the well-stocked restrooms. Most folks I encountered seemed friendly and I was happy not to encounter much late-night carousing, etc., which I've run into in some other spots on the Olympic Peninsula. But I was disappointed to find the campground choked with RVs running generators, their occupants elbowing rapaciously for the best campsites, dogs sometimes barking and allowed to run loose, etc. The campground hosts were barely civil and seemed to have received special training in how to be less than helpful to a camper seeking information. Overall, I found that the juice wasn't worth the squeeze in terms of camping at Kalaloch and will camp elsewhere next time.

reviews.author: Rebecca H.
reviews.text: This was a great campground!   Our site was clean and we loved the location to so many beaches and access to trails.  Only negatives were some campers had fires when there was a fire ban and no hand soap in the bathroom though we did have our own.

reviews.author: Tannia N.
reviews.text: I have been going to Kalaloch for over 70 years. The park used to be maintained very nicely however, today and for the past eight years this park has gone downhill. The sites are not maintained. The brush is overgrown weeds are everywhere. There’s no fresh rock to level the sites out, and the ashes are not cleared out of the fire pits this year. The fire pits were last used in August years before they weren’t used all summer and they were never emptied until the day after reservations ended. The only good thing about Kalaloch is that the bathrooms are very clean greatly appreciate those maintenance girls who clean the restrooms the compost is a joke. He does nothing and he has to be right whenever there’s a discussion with the guest not with me, but I’ve witnessed it with a bunch of guests having discussions with him while we were there The Campos worries if your tires are 1 inch over onto the main part of the road, but there’s no way to get any closer then we rented another site to put the vehicle in and in case our daughters came for the weekend and he said we can’t do that I think some of us that we’ve been coming for so long no the rules a little bit better than him not saying I’m a no at all, but he is just not the right person in my eyes to be a host for a beautiful park I wish and I pray that somebody can start maintaining the park on a regular Basis. My husband and I keep saying we would love to go there in volunteer just to clean it up and there’s no excuse why this cannot be done daily. They can blow an edge a little bit of the overgrown grass where people wanna put chairs around the campfire and blow the needles off of the site But the camp the Rangers and the hose say why do it we would just have to do it every day obviously they don’t want that part to be beautiful like it has been in the years

reviews.author: Kaila R.
reviews.text: This is our 32nd year camping at Kalaloch. We love it there.

reviews.author: Solomon C.
reviews.text: Legit right next to the bathroom so that was very convenient at night or early mornings. The steps to the beach by campsite A19 is less than a 3 min walk. This was very helpful and encouraging to spend more time at the beach while you're at the campground. I even had good enough service to Facetime so for beginners or people who are figuring out their way into nature, this is an easier spot to blend into. The campsite isn't the most private, but had enough space to feel like you're alone depending on how you set up. All in all a great campsite in my opinion for ease of access! Definitely go and see the Tree of life while you can and don’t miss sunset on the beach of course.

reviews.author: Christine C.
reviews.text: We were in D-25, view was amazing.

reviews.author: Heather B.
reviews.text: This is my 2nd time being here (1st time being 7 yrs ago) and it is still a great campground and the beach itself is beautiful.

reviews.author: Nikhil S.
reviews.text: Nice site in the middle of C loop surrounded by trees on three sides. Plenty of space to fit multiple tents and a canopy. Site comes with a fire pit and a concrete picnic table. Parking is 'street side' as opposed to a pull-in space; an RV would not fit here. Bathrooms and water are a 1-minute walk. The beach is a 2-3 minute walk away. The sound of the ocean is apparent in the campsite but you are far enough away for it to not be overpowering. You can hear cars passing on the highway but we did not find it to be an issue.

reviews.author: Hemakumar  J.
reviews.text: Best ocean view

reviews.author: Jacob M.
reviews.text: The campground and campsites are incredibly beautiful and right near the ocean. There is some noise from the highway, they don't have showers, and there bathrooms were run down with no soap or mechanism for washing your hands.

reviews.author: Timothy N.
reviews.text: Very nice camp site over looking the ocean.

reviews.author: Ana M.
reviews.text: All clean, well organized. Excellent location at the beach.

reviews.author: Catherine W.
reviews.text: Beautiful well kept sites, bathroom and fresh water facilities are clean and abundant and access to the glorious pacific coast is less than a 5 minute walk. Im already planning another visit.

reviews.author: James G.
reviews.text: Our campsite was nice. Other amenities were not up to normal expectations, lowering our rating. The camp water source for our end of the campground was turned off. We had to get water from the dump station. The hand dryer in the women’s bathroom did not work. The faucets in the men’s bathroom worked occasionally. The camp office was closed both days we were there. Budget cuts and layoffs are creating a negative experience in our national parks. Very sad situation.

reviews.author: Sarah B.
reviews.text: Firstly, the proximity of this campground to the beach was amazing. I gave this particular site, D39, only 3 stars because the website made it seem like you could pull your motorhome into the site, but you cannot. Our 24ft motorhome was able to parallel park at the end of the campsite by the road, but there was a curb blocking our vehicle from entering the site. I would recommend for tent camping or possibly combination of tent and motorhome.

reviews.author: Karla P.
reviews.text: Loved the privacy hedge around my tent site.  Snagged an oceanfront spot and had a wonderful sleep listening to the ocean.  campground was quiet, well-kept, and had easy access to the beach.  LOVED it, despite it's being in a part of the park that is pretty far from other things.

reviews.author: Julien L.
reviews.text: Great campsite by the water

reviews.author: Angkeabosh P.
reviews.text: The campground was very clean and peaceful.

reviews.author: Lisa B.
reviews.text: Bring soap for the bathroom and container for water to have at your campsite . Probably the most walkable and beautiful  each in Washington.

reviews.author: Andrea P.
reviews.text: Love this place!

reviews.author: Betzalel B.
reviews.text: One of the most beautiful campsite locations in America. while loops ABC are more densely, wooded and provide More shelter and a forest- like Campground experience, DEF Are pretty amazing in their own right. Site E11 is footsteps away from the cliff side overlooking the beach. Spectacular cmping experience.

reviews.author: Rachel H.
reviews.text: Ocean view campsites are the best!

reviews.author: Diana K.
reviews.text: Large flat plot with room for big tents or several small tents, which is rare at the campsite. Nicely shaded and not too far from bathroom. Unfortunately no kitchen sink and potable water. Road behind the site is kinda noisy but less than I expected.

reviews.author: Mike R.
reviews.text: The reduction in force for the Park Service Rangers and contractors is very obvious. The Rangers that are left are going over and beyond expectations to meet the needs of the campers. We heard two great evening presentations and spoke to another Ranger who was working very long hours to cover all the things that about three Rangers would have done in the past. And without the contractors the toilet faculties were not being serviced at all, making their use unpleasant. But the experience at Kalaloch was still great just because it is a great campground and the beach is wonderful. Don't fail to walk the nature trail across the highway. That's as much a part of the great experience of Kalaloch as the beach.

reviews.author: ANNIE K.
reviews.text: The most beautiful campsite in the country.

reviews.author: Beau V.
reviews.text: The campground is a beautiful spot in the trees. The beach is cool with tons of driftwood and the tree of life.

reviews.author: Kirk W.
reviews.text: The campground is great and access to the beach is the best. The only downside is that campsite D002 is NOT an RV site. The pad is so sloped that you’re not getting anywhere close to level unless you have hydraulic lifts, which we did not. Fortunately our traveling companions did, so we traded spots with them. Aside from that, the site is very nice and spacious.

reviews.author: Lee H.
reviews.text:
Very nice experience.  Well done and thanks for the great weather. 
Repair the steps maybe .

reviews.author: Pamela  H.
reviews.text: Site D030 had amazing views and was somewhat exposed to the ocean breeze which made putting up our tent a smidge harder than normal.  Of course, the ocean view more than made up for that fact.

reviews.author: Dante J.
reviews.text: We ended up staying in this campsite somewhat by chance, but it was such an ideal and beautiful camping spot, we hope to come back annually now!

reviews.author: Jeffra F.
reviews.text: Kalaloch is a sprawling campground, but the campsites are generously spaced out so that you still feel like you’re relatively secluded from other campers. There was surprisingly little noise after dark given the number of campsites that were occupied. The restroom facilities were also clean… just no hand soap! Easy access to the beach. There are some campsites facing the ocean with no vegetative obstruction. Reservations were very difficult to obtain regardless of the location of the campsite. Nevertheless, we noted numerous empty sites with “reserved” notices posted at their entrance but which remained unoccupied throughout the night and morning. Maybe the automatic cancellation deadline should go into effect at midnight on the day the reservation begins rather than noon on the following day. Seems overly generous given the demand for campsites. Access to First, Second, Third, and Fourth Beach up the road made for some nice variety as far as sunbathing, beachcombing, and tide pooling  were concerned. I give this campground high marks overall.

reviews.author: Patrick K.
reviews.text: Nice spot next to the beach entrance. The beach is beautiful!

reviews.author: Anthony I.
reviews.text: Kalaloch is hard to beat as far as camping on the Olympic Peninsula goes - the proximity of all sites to the beach is just awesome. Reservations fill up fast for the summer but recommend using availability alerts and something should come up!

reviews.author: Paul B.
reviews.text: Nice and calm camping spot. Close to the road bit still quiet at night. Beautiful beach.

reviews.author: Sara W.
reviews.text: The campsites are well maintained, the ranger talks were a highlight! The beach access was convenient. We were disappointed there was no soap in the restroom (C loop) and the restroom in A loop was closed. Only one bathroom stall had toilet paper half way through our 3 day stay. There’s also graffiti on the traffic sign directly across from the beach access closest to A loop - seems like something the campsite should take care of right away to discourage more graffiti. We will come back, but hoping some of these maintenance issues are improved next time!

reviews.author: Tara P.
reviews.text: This place is really really nice for a getaway, lots of beach time and viewing of tree of life. Such a magical place!

reviews.author: Laura S.
reviews.text: The bathroom facility closest to this site is also used by the day users, which makes it busy. You can walk a little further to two other facilities. This also means it’s close to the beach access entrance, which is nice (but also noisy).  The site is small relative to the other beach adjacent sites, with little privacy - but it’s overlooking the beach! Camped in a rooftop tent, so we had a perfect view. Would recommend for a short stay.

reviews.author: Christopher H.
reviews.text: Campsite was great but extremely close to the next one. The bathrooms are in extreme need of repairs.

reviews.author: matthew s.
reviews.text: Big site and super close to the beach. Awesome!

reviews.author: Kelly B.
reviews.text:
The campground is always awesome. Our campsite was a good size for our two small tents and chairs and didn’t feel cramped. 
Neighbors are far enough away that you don’t feel them breathing down your neck. 
There is road noise for those sensitive and I believe it’s that way no matter where your site is located in the campground. 
Shady site just the way I like it! 
It was 60° in August so come prepared for any weather. I recommend layers. 
FYI there is a tsunami siren test every 1st Monday of the month at noon. Kinda spooky if you didn’t hear the announcement that it was a test. 😊

reviews.author: Kim H.
reviews.text: Spent 1 night in 034. Nice campsite, great location - near the beach trail, bathrooms, and water. NOT on the bluff side, with a campsite behind it (so, not the most private). Bathrooms were functional but VERY tired and old. Would definitely camp at Kalaloch again!

reviews.author: Lisa B.
reviews.text: Beautiful spot!

reviews.author: Tamara J.
reviews.text: We had a great time at Kalaloch this year.  Our family has been coming here for about 50 years.  My only issue was access to potable water from the D loop as well as dish washing access (and realize it's not the parks fault for water mains being messed up)  The staff was super helpful to us in being able to release one of the days on our reservation because of a no-show, so someone else could use it.  Kalaloch is the BEST sandy beach in the PNW!!  That's why reservations are so difficult, but we are grateful to have been able to grab them this year!

reviews.author: Amy K.
reviews.text: Another terrific stay at Kalaloch!

reviews.author: Earl B.
reviews.text: Please help us maintain the park by keeping a clean and secure (coyotes) campsite at all times.

reviews.author: Jennifer  B.
reviews.text: This campground had way too many sites for the area. Sites were tiny and packed in close. The beachfront sites may have been better, but our site was in the middle of one of the loops. The location of the campground was great, but we ended up leaving before spending the night because it was just too many people condensed into a small area.

reviews.author: Elaine S.
reviews.text: Loved it, our site and the relaxed atmosphere. Great for family as well. Will be back again.

reviews.author: Rosalie L.
reviews.text: Camping within view of the beach and just a ten minute walk away inside seriously beautiful moss covered trees. The only downside was there was no room for our tent. We had to wedge it between the picnic table and the bushes and get scratched in the bushes trying to get in our tent. It needs to be trimmed back more. Other sites have much more room. Don't use this particular one if you have more than a small two person tent.

reviews.author: Brad W.
reviews.text:
Kalaloch is a beautiful campground.
Clean bathrooms

reviews.author: Sai Jyothish M.
reviews.text: The site we stayed at was peaceful with just a bit of crunch underfoot, and it was spacious enough to fit both our tents—a 6-person and a 3-person.

reviews.author: Linda F.
reviews.text: We love Kalaloch camping! Very disappointed that the first bathroom in the A-Loop was closed. This is very frustrating! It's been in disrepair for YEARS! Please just get it fixed or replaced!! Thank you! Otherwise fine visit.

reviews.author: Roxanne E.
reviews.text:
Campsites are wonderful but I was surprised paved parts were not cleaned off between visitors. This park is very similar to GREENPOINT campground on Vancouver Island, which we frequent so I couldn’t help comparing the upkeep.
Also, the one large bathroom has been out for months - a stairway to the beach the same. I found it amusing that someone with more lumber and nails to further block the access when he could be repairing it instead?
Walking north to the end of the beach at low tide is a must. 
Perhaps a sign that says “Please don’t chase the birds on the beach” might stop people's kids from doing this. Also need NO OVERNIGHT PARKING on overlook to beach at area A. Totally full at 7 am.
Staff were very kind. Will definitely return to this beautiful area.

reviews.author: Mason W.
reviews.text: This site was a in a great location, friendly folks around, good hiking, beach walks, and access to the tree of life. I would bring bigger tent stakes, the ground is very hard to get tent spikes in. Highly recommend this lovely campground!

reviews.author: Grace W.
reviews.text: The beach here is stunning and there is easy access, but some of the spots on the campsite are right by the road. Traffic can drive by pretty fast including trucks which can be disruptive.

reviews.author: Narciso  C.
reviews.text: Restrooms doesn’t work no water garbages in that garbage bin doesn’t pick up smell so very bad never took care for the facility employees very bad and camp site never trimming bushes!

reviews.author: Lorri P.
reviews.text: OMH we loved this campground! So beautiful, loved the stairs to the beach and we got a wonderful site overlooking the water. Hope it doesn't erode more! The bathrooms were clean, sites big and separated. Really enjoyed our stay!

reviews.author: K.
reviews.text: One of my favorite!

reviews.author: Bree A.
reviews.text: Wow! The view of Kalaloch beach from our campsite was amazing. This beach is so incredible. The campground itself is well maintained. Wished there was a little more privacy between our site (D25) and the site directly behind us but other than that, this was one of our absolute favorite campgrounds!

reviews.author: Daniel R.
reviews.text: Beautiful beach with wonderful sunsets. We used a tent spot at campground and enjoyed grilling steaks on the fire. The lodge about 1/4 mile away serves pretty good lunches. Bathroom facilities at the campground are just OK.

reviews.author: Scott V.
reviews.text: While the location is great with close proximity to the wide beach, the infrastructure was in poor condition.  One restroom (out of 5) was closed due to water problems.   There were sometimes a waiting line to get into the restrooms.  The one closest to us had only one toilet in the men's room.  There was no soap in the bathrooms.  Water stations for filling water bottles had been installed at the restroom locations but none of them were in service.  The sole source of drinking water was at the RV pump out station.  Because of high use, the area around the spigot was flooded.   The central stairs to the beach were washed out so you had to walk to one of the remaining two.  On all the campground instructions there was strict rules about parking on pavement only and the maximum length of vehicle and campers at each site.  These rules were not followed or enforced.   Perhaps these problems are the result of a cut in funding, but it is a shame to see such a historic campground in such a dilapidated state.

reviews.author: Kanda H.
reviews.text: We stayed here two nights. The first night was amazing. Absolutely well kept excellent experience and campground site. The second night at this site was not great. No privacy at all. Very small campsite. Nowhere to fit tent had to move it to the parking area which made it difficult to park our car. The biggest problem was the broken fire grill that only had three metal spokes remaining making it very difficult to cook our meals. We had an ocean view, but was greatly obscured by poison oak.

reviews.author: Kanda H.
reviews.text: The site I stayed at was private and wonderful! View of the ocean, pretty clean bathrooms and lots of space.

reviews.author: Pierre S.
reviews.text: Enjoyed our stay BUT we found site A24 quite difficult to back into, even with our 21ft trailer : back-in sites are usually “driven past” and then backed into, but this one is the opposite and required some “borderline jack-knifing”

reviews.author: brooke  j.
reviews.text: What a beautiful spot. The ocean is a view, but there was a bushes in way to see it. I climbed on top of my car roof rack to be able see the ocean at sunset. It was so beautiful. I loved being able to hear the ocean all night. There was steps not too far to be able to go down to beach. One of my favorite campsites.

reviews.author: Abigail E.
reviews.text: Campground was absolutely beautiful, our site was pretty close up on other sites, but that’s camping generally. Only problem we ran into were the bathrooms. The bathroom in one of the loops was closed, so everyone in the two lower loops had to use the same bathroom resulting in it becoming extremely unclean and without certain items necessary to use it. Apart from that, the nature and climate were very desirable. Great overall experience!

reviews.author: Jeffery O.
reviews.text: Beautiful area, but tent spot was super small and area was so close to the main road we decided not to stay the night after a couple days of backpacking. Went down to the awesome sandy beach to dip our toes in the water before heading out and had to navigate a severely broken down “staircase” to and from. Surprised with how popular the campground is that towards the end of July the pathway down to the beach would not be more accessible.

reviews.author: Desiree W.
reviews.text: This campground is set steps from beach access, in a wooded area. The fog tends to roll in from the beach often, so be prepared with layers and things being a bit moist! The facilities (bathrooms, water etc) were good.

reviews.author: Amy A.
reviews.text: Stayed in site C5. Looking at other sites, this one was not the best but it was certainly better than others. Fit a big tent. It was close to the bathroom (but not close enough to hear or smell it) but otherwise very private. Lots of vegetation gave privacy and the ocean covered most of the sound of other campers. Close walk to the beach. Overall, very clean campground. Would stay here again.

reviews.author: Larissa H.
reviews.text: We really enjoyed camping here and will again if we are lucky enough to score reservations. The proximity to the beach is fantastic and for us was the highlight. If you have a large tent, like we did, pay attention to tent pad size in the description. Our site F2 was in direct view of our neighbors. Luckily that wasn’t an issue since they had an RV, but something to note. Bathroom availability can be a bit of an issue. There were only two stalls per gender to service a pretty large area. It really just depends on how many people are tent camping vs RVing. When we went there were a lot of tent campers so the restrooms got crowded and only one sink worked. Another thing was getting water. Our location by the restrooms was out of service so we needed to go to the next restroom over and that was a pretty far walk to carry water. Those issues were really not a big deal for us, but just giving others a heads up. Overall a really great campground and we hope to camp here again!

reviews.author: Marjory C.
reviews.text: Great campground! It’s our favorite.

reviews.author: Mic G.
reviews.text: Clean, maintained, up to date facilities (with lots of wall outlets!). Lovely beach with great access. Felt perfectly safe leaving belongings while we went sightseeing, and guests were courteous (except for the one guy with the LED headlamp that was bright enough to light up the inside of our tent like day time from two spots away 😆😆) and maintained their spots very well.

reviews.author: Christina C.
reviews.text: Was there for one night. If you like white noise when you sleep you’re going to love the sound of the waves flowing in from the ocean. Great spot to experience the coast at Olympic National Park!

reviews.author: Ruth L.
reviews.text: It took us several years to finally successfully reserve a camping site. It was frustrating to see several unoccupied sites while there knowing our struggles to reserve an open site. I suggest that if a party does not arrive at a site on their arrival date by 7:00pm, they be fined  at least $200 and the site be given away to another party. (If the fines are petty, people won’t care) This would also help funding the upkeep for the park.

reviews.author: Diane L.
reviews.text: Beach was amazing.  The nature trail was also great

reviews.author: Ben T.
reviews.text: Great, private spots easily walkable to wonderful beach.  So nice!

reviews.author: Sarah H.
reviews.text: We had great proximity to the beach, it was very quiet and we could hear the waves! Short walk to the tree of Life. There is a decent space between campgrounds so you don't have to be right up on your neighbor!

reviews.author: Charlotte S.
reviews.text: Nice campground. Spacious area.

reviews.author: Allison A.
reviews.text: Great site we were able to snag the day of on the weekend. C18 was big enough for 2 separate 2-person tents and nicely secluded from neighbouring sites by vegetation.

reviews.author: Kay O.
reviews.text: During our stay we had an incident with lost keys. The camp hosts were extremely helpful and kind. Luckily the keys were found. The week stay was wonderful as usual.

reviews.author: Angela S.
reviews.text: I've been going to Kalaloch for 40 years and though some years we get luckier than others with the weather, I am always happy and contented there.  We explored Third Beach this time, and it was just gorgeous.  Kalaloch is unapologetically rustic, which is what one should expect for The-middle-of-nowhere, Washington Coast.  I love that it has not changed much at all in decades.  Note for newcomers: bring your own hand soap to the campground!

reviews.author: Demory H.
reviews.text:
Gorgeous jumping off spot for seeing the park and with excellent views. 

Pay attention to your site details as ours was listed as “standard non electric” but then said lower that there was no tent pad. We made it work with a small car and our tent on the parking spot but some sites are much bigger. 

It can be kind of noisy with RV generators

reviews.author: madison s.
reviews.text: Beaches are amazing! It’s a very clean camp ground!

reviews.author: Melissa B.
reviews.text: Had a great experience camping here. The ground at site A048 was very flat for a tent and there were enough trees to feel privacy from how close the neighboring sites are. Expect bathroom doesn't have soap. I was nervous about arriving around 8p instead of our 12p check in time since we were traveling, but we just drove right in to our spot without difficulty.

reviews.author: Danny H.
reviews.text: Great location and sufficient camp sites. We love the proximity to so many fun activities. Facilities are clean & easy to access

reviews.author: Kelby B.
reviews.text: Nice quiet camp site, short walk to beach. Bathrooms leave a lot to be desired

reviews.author: Caitlin C.
reviews.text: Kalaloch is a beautiful area. This campsite was very close to beach and the Lodge with a camp store and restaurant. I'm taking one star away for the proximity to the highway.

reviews.author: Glen-Erik C.
reviews.text: beautiful campsite with oceanview

reviews.author: Stephanie Z.
reviews.text: Love this campground!

reviews.author: Scott  H.
reviews.text: This is a gorgeous campground! The beach is beautiful as are the trees surrounding the campground. It felt very private

reviews.author: David W.
reviews.text: Great location and sea views and a cool ocean side campground.  Highly recommend.

reviews.author: Amy H.
reviews.text: You really couldn’t ask for a more beautiful location! The ocean view is absolutely amazing. It was disappointing that there was no hand soap in any of the bathrooms nor any kind of paper towel or hand dryer and only a trashcan part of the time. It was also disappointing that when we left for a day excursion and came back to our campsite our firewood, bottled water and sodas had all been taken. We were car camping so no tent was set up. Perhap folks didn’t realize we were coming back but either way was it not only a disappointment but very inconvenient since buying water, firewood and soda is not available once the little store at the lodge has closed for the day. Either way, I would certainly return to this campground, but would not leave any of my belongings behind.

reviews.author: Amurta N.
reviews.text: Great location and decent sized campground. Bathrooms were clean and well maintained.

reviews.author: Peggy L.
reviews.text:
Have been camping at Kalaloch for 70 years! Love the rugged coast, cool weather and sun in late AM through rest of day. 
Enjoyed going to beaches. Ranger low tide walk and ranger talks. The whale talk was ex excellent.

reviews.author: Gina E.
reviews.text: This was a lovely campground.  We could hear the waves from our campsite, which was so calming.  Neighbors were polite, and the rangers and volunteers were so wonderful.  We had a great camping trip.

reviews.author: Roberto G.
reviews.text: A short hike to ocean. Beautiful. Not too many bugs. My campsite was close to highway but wasn't bad.

reviews.author: Cindy T.
reviews.text: Infrastructure desperately needs work. Not enough toilets and those that were there are run down with no soap and inoperative air dryers. One whole toilet building was closed. The amphitheater needs to be painted. The lodge looks tired and old. And the staff looked like they  were sparse and overworked. That all said, our campsite was clean as was the beach.

reviews.author: Johanna S.
reviews.text: Most amazing camp spot, better than I could have imagined 😍 the beauty of nature in this area is absolutely stunning. I wish I could stay in all the different spots to get both the cozy rainforest like spots as well as the water front sunny spots ☀️

reviews.author: China  W.
reviews.text: This site is located right next to 101. However it was a holiday weekend, and I felt it was still very quiet! Definitely a small space and not for a larger tent! This campground one of my top 5!

reviews.author: Yaelle B.
reviews.text: Very good place to look at sunset

reviews.author: Hilah S.
reviews.text: Kalaloch is a beautiful campground and we have visited several times; however, this time only one dishwashing station was functional for the whole campground.

reviews.author: Virginia P.
reviews.text: Such a beautiful spot with the vast beach and setting in the Olympics. Rugged beauty.

reviews.author: Roshan S.
reviews.text: We had the best experience here, out of all the other campgrounds we stayed in. Our site faced the ocean, and we slept to the sound of it.. so relaxing. There are plenty of bathrooms nearby.

reviews.author: AMEY UDAY P.
reviews.text: Step out of your campsite onto a pristine beach!

reviews.author: Aaron G.
reviews.text: Site was tight but as advertised.  Location is great right on the bluff.  It would be nice to have showers but knew there weren’t any at this site.  Overall great experience.

reviews.author: cyndi c.
reviews.text: As always a beautiful place to visit. With a few sites closed due to bluff erosion, it actually opens up more views for all walking by. Can't say 5* due to there not being showers, that addition would make a HUGE improvement for restroom cleanliness.

reviews.author: Kimberly H.
reviews.text: My space was small, but since I camp in my minivan it wasn’t a big deal. My site backed right up to the cliff overlooking the beach. Nearby stairs/trail gave access to the beach. Small but decent flush toilet bathroom nearby. Only wish I could have stayed longer!

reviews.author: ronald h.
reviews.text: Noisy camp site near road. Lots of empty campsites that had been reserved but not used. Broken bathroom without a backup

reviews.author: Pat M.
reviews.text: We were lucky to reserve a campsite right on the bluff with a view of the water and beach.  Our trip was planned to take advantage of the tides being extra low, allowing us to spend a lot of time walking on the beaches and to visit the tidal pools at the north end of the Kalaloch beach.

reviews.author: Sarah V.
reviews.text:
We stayed at site 42 in Kalaloch Campground and it was absolutely perfect for tent camping. The site felt incredibly secluded, giving the sense of camping deep in nature, even though the campground is fairly large. It was quiet, peaceful, and spacious, making it one of our favorite spots of the trip.

It’s just a short walk to the beach, where you can catch stunning sunsets, and Kalaloch Lodge is nearby with an excellent restaurant if you’re looking to enjoy a nice meal without cooking. This location is also ideal for exploring the southwest side of Olympic National Park, including Ruby Beach and the Hoh Rainforest.

Highly recommend Kalaloch campground if you're looking for solitude, beauty, and easy access to all the highlights of the coast.

reviews.author: David G.
reviews.text: The beach was clean and gorgeous. Mostly cloudy during our stay, but the marine layer burned off one day to give us a clear sky for sunset and at night for stargazing at the beach. the Tree of Life is by the campsite, if not RIGHT below the main day use parking lot.

reviews.author: Rachel M.
reviews.text: Loved this site and campground. Bathrooms were super clean. The view from site 25 was absolutely amazing. This site abuts the campsite behind it without much privacy, which were not be fun if you had a bad group. Fortunately, everyone was respectable here.

reviews.author: Gary S.
reviews.text: Small sites in close proximity to both the road and the beach.   Campground was very lush and we loved that we could hike the beaches directly from our campground.  No showers, but the restrooms were clean.  Working dump station was available too.

reviews.author: Winkie M.
reviews.text: One of the best campsites in the entire campground. Very private. The view is small but that's not a bad thing as it does get windy. Small site though, one 3 person tent is fine but 2 tents or a bigger tent will be a squeeze. No AT&T cell signal at all, but if you hop over to the loop E/F bathroom it's barely usable.

reviews.author: Mary D.
reviews.text: This campsite was amazing! Plenty of space for our family, and it was incredible being so close to the beach, while also being among the trees! We can't wait to come back.

reviews.author: Victoria H.
reviews.text: The parking pad at A 19 and those close by was angled such that a trailer was impossible to back into without driving into the grass/ bushes. In general,  very small site only accommodating one tent. Loop A bathrooms were closed and water was located at the restrooms only. However, gorgeous views of the ocean with a pathway to the beach 200 feet away. Gorgeous!

reviews.author: Brendan W.
reviews.text: Convenient access to beaches to visit tidepools at low tide.

reviews.author: Lisa V.
reviews.text: Nice site at the ocean, nice trees

reviews.author: Amber S.
reviews.text: Excellent camping spot! Perfect amount of privacy even next to the bathroom.

reviews.author: Wesley S.
reviews.text:
We got a four-day reservation, and the available site was pleasant, but nearer to the highway than we would have preferred. (Traffic noise was minimal after dark, though.)  The parking pad was almost perfectly level. The space was clean. Restrooms were well maintained. The nearest trail to the beach (near the "Tree of Life") was closed due to erosion ... but that was okay, as we needed the walking. 

In the morning, everything was wet from ocean mist. If we had been tenting, this could have been a difficulty.

reviews.author: Paul C.
reviews.text: Clean, private spot right on the bluff.

reviews.author: john s.
reviews.text: there was some one in our camp site, had to give another one not as good.

reviews.author: Ann B.
reviews.text: This is a beautiful campground.  It was our second time camping here, this time in early June.  The weather off the ocean is a bit of a wildcard, but we were prepared for it rain or shine. Luckily we had a bit of both. Our camp spot is a bit on the small side if you have a lot of tents.  We squeezed in two small and two medium sized tents with some room to spare. Bathroom are pretty good, no warm water, but they are clean and functional. The fact the campground is only about 1/4 mile from the Kalalock Lodge is lovely.  We got soft serve ice-cream and extra firewood, which was a pleasant surprise.

reviews.author: Ty S.
reviews.text: I only stayed for one night, but it was great. The bathrooms were clean, the site was clean when I arrived. There were a lot of people staying that night however it never felt crowded, which was nice.

reviews.author: Nicole B.
reviews.text: Such a beautiful place!

reviews.author: Heidi B.
reviews.text:
5/5 – Stunning Bluff Views & Clean, Peaceful Campground

Kalaloch Campground is absolutely beautiful. We stayed on a bluff site and were blown away by the ocean views—sunshine and sea breeze made it feel like something out of a postcard. It’s a quick and easy walk to the famous Tree of Life, and we loved having direct access to the beach. Sand, sunshine, and serenity were in abundance.

The facilities were impressively clean, including the bathrooms, and the ranger on duty was kind and helpful. We had booked two nights at two different sites (since that’s all that was available), but due to travel delays, we unfortunately missed our first night. I really wish there was a way to cancel or release a site last-minute so someone else could enjoy it—it’s such a shame for it to sit empty!

That said, we truly enjoyed our time there and just wish there had been more availability so we could’ve stayed longer. Highly recommend this campground, especially the bluff sites—they’re unforgettable.

reviews.author: Allen W.
reviews.text: Excellent campground very close to the beach. Lots of families. Some sites are small while others are spacious. Be sure to bring soap as there aren’t any dispensers in the bathrooms.

reviews.author: sandra  j.
reviews.text: none

reviews.author: Hannah S.
reviews.text: It was lovely!

reviews.author: Natalie C.
reviews.text: This spot can comfortably accommodate 4 people. Perfect fairy foliage amongst this site. The lodge is conveniently located nearby in case you forget any necessities. There's also maintenance onsite that can assist with some auto issues. Loved the location by the ocean and 1 hr away from Hoh Rainforest. Sometimes there was a motorcycle driving by a bit loudly since this site is near the road, but that didn't bother me too much.

reviews.author: Barbara M.
reviews.text: Loved being a walk away from the beach, and wind-protected by beautiful, huge trees!  We had beautiful weather.  The only downside was the condition of the bathrooms, which need updating. Note to E.V. drivers:  free chargers available at Kalaloch Lodge.  Favorite beach nearby was beach #4.

reviews.author: Brizaida  M.
reviews.text: Safe place to stay.

reviews.author: Dominic C.
reviews.text: For $24 I'd hope to have showers but realistically that's no big deal. What is a huge deal is paying $24 and not $17 like other sites that have pit toilets and no showers but not providing soap at all. Prices need to go down if no soap is provided.

reviews.author: Fred S.
reviews.text: great beach access, private sites, bathrooms need updating

reviews.author: Jessica K.
reviews.text: We had a lovely time here! So much beauty to take in, sunsets on the beach were the best!

reviews.author: Grace M.
reviews.text: Oceanfront site. Only downside is that it is not a very private campground. But the views make up for that!

reviews.author: James  T.
reviews.text: Great campground, lovely beach, epic scenery, clean bathrooms, my site was sizeable but driving around I saw some were rather small, the beach access is great and the roads are well maintained!

reviews.author: Emma C.
reviews.text: Beautiful location!

reviews.author: Jennifer  W.
reviews.text: This is my favorite place!!! This campsite was beautiful and conveniently located neat the restroom and the beach path. Beautiful, well maintained, quiet, picturesque. Couldn't have asked for a better trip.

reviews.author: Caleb P.
reviews.text:
So many of the sites were 'reserved' and no one ever showed up.  
I appreciated the reservation system but not having a way for sites to be released for walk ups is incredibly frustrating.

reviews.author: Terry L.
reviews.text: This is an absolutely beautiful campground loved it here, right on the beach, with the tree of life.

reviews.author: Jane D.
reviews.text: The beach is always beautiful at Kalaloch.  What I don't get are the empty sites with reservation only signs that don't get filled.  If you look on the website all sites are reserved until the season ends in Sept.  That is not the case.  Also the promotion of the "tree of life" which years age never had a name, is falling down and hordes of day trippers run to grab a picture and then leave.  The staircase out of the day use lot is cordoned off as it is falling off but people climb it anyway.  A tourist trap!

reviews.author: Jennifer  S.
reviews.text: Beautiful location!

reviews.author: Patrick J.
reviews.text: Great location and well maintained camp ground. Be aware no showers or hot water.

reviews.author: Griet D.
reviews.text: Site was clean and the beach access was very close and accessible. It was only a slight downhill, Nothing that would tire you out. The campground was scenic with all the tall trees and then the sun coming through in the morning and the evening. It is a big campground so expect some activity, the sites are close together, but they do offer privacy.There are a couple of sites that are beachfront and closed due to potential hazards however, we use them to watch the sunset. There is a dump station on the other side of the campgrounds which was I believe 5 or $10.

reviews.author: Ryan V.
reviews.text: Area and being close to the beach is amazing. Tree of life is a short walk away. The only real issues are the size of campsites and the bathrooms. There is no soap in the bathrooms and they are not the newest. They are maintained to a certain extent.

reviews.author: Aleksandra  F.
reviews.text: Great as always

reviews.author: Donna C.
reviews.text: Although the campground is close to hwy 101, it’s a quiet and peaceful location.  Every campsite is close to the beach and you fall asleep to the sound of the waves.

reviews.author: John R.
reviews.text: Very convenient location to access the southwest beaches of Olympic National Park.  We loved our site, set among mossy trees, easy walking to the bathroom and the beach.  Wonderful to pitch a tent with the sounds of the Pacific Ocean.

reviews.author: Susan S.
reviews.text: Campsites are nice. Bathrooms need updating. 2 stalls for all the campsites in the loop isn't enough. Great to be steps away from the beach.

reviews.author: Zoran L.
reviews.text: This spot is fine, although it's a bit close to other spots. The main issue is that it's right across the road from some kind of a pump that turns on at random times (like 9pm or 5am) and is audible even through earplugs.

reviews.author: Aaron C.
reviews.text: Excellent campsite right by the ocean you can hear it even if your site is not right on the ocean.

reviews.author: Casey W.
reviews.text: A beautiful stay the location could not have been more perfect we watched the sun go down over the ocean and ate breakfast with a bald eagle right above our site. Close to the tree of life entrance and a relaxing walk on the beach.

reviews.author: Lisa K.
reviews.text: Nice private sites.  But there is road noise, THE DUMP station is not included in site cost (never saw that before), and the bathrooms were FILTHY.

reviews.author: Steve B.
reviews.text: Small site with limited view due to untrimmed bushes when were there. However, it is only a short walk to beach access.

reviews.author: michael m.
reviews.text: One bathroom was out, but the Park Ranger was an incredibly good, friendly, and helpful person who knew the answer to every question our group had. Really appreciate her!

reviews.author: Jennifer H.
reviews.text: One of my favorite places to camp!

reviews.author: edward m.
reviews.text:
One of the bathrooms was out of order, which is a problem. However, the bigger issue is the overgrown sites. There’s no way to park multiple vehicles as advertised. The beach was barely visible from the site, even though the photos showed a much better view. The site description claims that the campsite is flat, but it’s not!

If the site is open, I suggest you take some time to maintain it.

reviews.author: Peter  M.
reviews.text: Amazing location right on the beach. Campsites are clean and well maintained

reviews.author: Mary W.
reviews.text: Beautiful place to camp and enjoy walks on the beach and access to hiking nearby.

reviews.author: Alicia  B.
reviews.text: Beautiful scenery, clean campsites, and every site is amazing! One of the best in WA for sure!!!

reviews.author: Aleksandra  F.
reviews.text: It was a nice spot, I’m absolutely in love with this campground

reviews.author: Mary N.
reviews.text: Simple camping on the coast.  We had a pathway to an ocean view in site A-11 which took securing 6 mos to the minute ahead of time.  But there were free spots when we arrived the Tuesday after Memorial Day.  We walked a few hundred feet south to the beach access from which we could walk the beach below our site.  Heads up to anyone interested in Tidal Pool exploring.  We had no cell signal but had pulled the tide schedule ahead of time and knew from our trusty National Park book that the nearest great spot was north at Beach 4, just north of mile marker 160.  Take the path down to the beach and then get yourself to the big rock outcroppings to the right.  The pools and rocks have more sea stars and anemones than those direction in front of the path.

reviews.author: Lori P.
reviews.text: Amazing views and a nice beach.

reviews.author: David H.
reviews.text: This is a nice campground but I fear that the National Park maintenance is going downhill.

reviews.author: Sandra O.
reviews.text: Ruby Beach at low tide!

reviews.author: Melanie C.
reviews.text: Beautiful site, helpful volunteer at checkin.

reviews.author: Narciso  C.
reviews.text: Bathroom out of service

reviews.author: Darla M.
reviews.text: Site E001 worked well for me and my dog but would be quite small for a family tent. It is a parallel parking situation so vehicle is close to the road. Nice to hear the ocean waves!

reviews.author: Kim S.
reviews.text: What a beautiful campground!  We very much enjoyed the beauty and being close to the beach.  It was almost full, but we hardly noticed we had neighbors due to the vegetation and quiet surroundings. The bathrooms were clean and comfortable.  We hope to return someday.

reviews.author: David H.
reviews.text: It rained one night.

reviews.author: Katie R.
reviews.text: Spots near the road (predictably) have road noise, would reserve closer to the ocean. But overall a great experience, easy beach access, clean

reviews.author: Katie S.
reviews.text: The view was incredible and it was awesome to sleep near the ocean. The campsites were relatively private although they were a little bit overgrown. There was one non-working bathroom facility while we were there, but there was another one close by.  One downside of the bathroom facilities are that there are no showers. There is a store a couple miles down the road to get everything you need minus the ice machine being broken. Overall, the stay was great and we would consider coming back!

reviews.author: Arpit R.
reviews.text: Amazing campground which quick access to the beach, toilets could have been cleaner but hey, we are outdoors so can't get everything

reviews.author: John R.
reviews.text: The campsite was clean.  Most bathrooms were open and clean.  Other campers were courteous and respectful.

reviews.author: Michael  W.
reviews.text: Clean and quiet campground. Close to the visitor center and central to many hikes/nature walks. It was a very quiet night and very dark. So no light pollution for those who stargaze.

reviews.author: Erika S.
reviews.text: Gorgeous camp spot!

reviews.author: Kylie K.
reviews.text: This place is amazing, right on the beach, I would recommend getting a spot closer to ocean, but I was in Loop A on the back side and it was very easy to watch the sunset. Highly recommend.

reviews.author: Achim W.
reviews.text: Es fehlten Duschen.
