reviews.text: Beautiful location.  Great hiking.  Well maintained campgrounds with clean bathrooms.

reviews.author: Jeff Y.
reviews.text: Great spot, views of the ocean.

reviews.author: Keegan S.
reviews.text: Stayed B11. While not direct beach view, it was about a 10 second walk to the beach entrance and it was a private site with all the trees

reviews.author: Julia I.
reviews.text:
Lovely campsite steps from the beach. Some sites have greater privacy than others, I especially liked a few ocean-facing ones on loop A. 
Driveway lengths vary, make sure to check your specific site. We wanted to buy firewood from the campsite hosts but they weren’t present, and there was no note on when they’ll be back, so maybe get your firewood before you get there.

reviews.author: Rachel O.
reviews.text: Kalaloch doesn’t disappoint.  Getting A19 was a welcome surprise. The site is convenient to beach access and restrooms.  Best part is it’s private and has enough around it to shield you from some of the wind. When I say private, the ranger called to see if I was coming as she missed my tent set up when doing site checks!  I’d recommend coming during the week when there are more sites available to choose from; also tends to be more peaceful.

reviews.author: Alice F.
reviews.text: Our experience at Kalaloch Campground was fantastic. I am so thankful for our National Parks. They are a treasure worth funding!

reviews.author: Rebecca W.
reviews.text: We had a quick stay at Kalaloch, but it had everything we needed - beautiful beach, showers, dump station, and easy to pull into camping space. We have a 26 ft RV, and had no problems at our site in B loop

reviews.author: Brenda M.
reviews.text:
Campground is beautiful as it is near the ocean
We enjoyed our stay
Would like to see the staircase leading down to the beach repaired, one woman with arthritis nearly fell going down broken uneven steps
Bathroom needs updates, broken tiles etc. it was nice that someone had liquid soap in women’s bathroom, but none in men’s restroom per my husband

reviews.author: Sarah R.
reviews.text: This is a beautiful place, and overall a nice campground. Our site, D027, had great beach access. However ... it's a lousy tent site. There's very little room for a tent, and when it rains, the water from the road runs right through it.

reviews.author: Eric W.
reviews.text: Beautiful location and convenient to other coastal features

reviews.author: Greg N.
reviews.text: Discover a fantastic destination! We loved the beach nearby—it was the perfect place to see the beautiful ocean and hike around the coast.

reviews.author: Becky W.
reviews.text: Beautiful, quiet campground with the occasional highway sound if closer to the road. Friendly and helpful rangers.

reviews.author: Darren J.
reviews.text:
E Loop is a small loop of sites, not a lot of privacy. No block from wind, strategic placement of gear is required.
 Still a good camping site, E6.

reviews.author: Darren J.
reviews.text:
A8 was a surprisingly good site. Great proximity to bathroom, dishwashing, closest to beach access for that tree everyone wants to see. Had to walk past amphitheater area to get to beach access, adding to convenience. Site A8 also had decent privacy. Look at the map and it looks like a busy location, which it is, although the back in parking is aligned for maximum privacy. 
Being not located directly on the beach side, the trees provide a decent block from the wind.

reviews.author: Tiffany L.
reviews.text: One of my favorite places to camp in Washington!

reviews.author: nancy f.
reviews.text:
When i booked online and did not realize that the sites were drive throughs. The sites were not accommodating for a pop-up Eurovan. I felt like the staff were reluctant to move me and I was very disappointed the next morning when there were so many empty sites. I know it is the end of the season and everybody is tired 
 but a little bit more help on their part would have been appreciated

reviews.author: Lynanne Y.
reviews.text: We had a great one-night stay!  Clean bathrooms plus a spacious and clear site. We had a little bit of a hard time finding the spot because the loops are a bit confusing in the dark but once settled it was a great night!

reviews.author: Vit K.
reviews.text: Excellent spot, only way to make it better would be to add power.

reviews.author: James S.
reviews.text: The setting was spectacular at first look but there were a lot of small things that kept it from keeping up with that. First is that it rained the second night and if I hadn't been camping suspended, I would have been sleeping in a small lake. You would think a bluff top site would have some drainage. The second issue is that the nearest working water spigot was over in the A loop. Other than that, the bathrooms were clean. It was mostly quiet. View was nice as was the sound of the ocean at night.

reviews.author: Robert Y.
reviews.text: Facilities are poorly maintained for a State Campground in a National Park.  There was no soap in the washrooms, which results in poor hygiene safety.

reviews.author: Dean J.
reviews.text: Clean and beautiful
Very easy eccess to the beach ( tree of life)

reviews.author: Susan B.
reviews.text: Beautiful location.  Perfect for peaceful sleeping among the trees.  Wide beaches invite long walks.  Everything was very clean.

reviews.author: James B.
reviews.text: Walk the beach at low tide and check out the tide pools.  Nice cool ocean breeze.  We stayed in A8 in a 25ft camper trailer. Very shady.

reviews.author: Darcy V.
reviews.text:
The location and setting are beautiful. The cabin had an odd configuration, one area with a bed, futon and dining/cooking area separated by a partial wall from the second bed. The bathroom was off of area with the second bed, so no private areas.  An issue with cleaning was promptly resolved by the friendly staff. 

The lodge had only a small common area by the check in counter with a limited view.  The restaurant in the lodge had great fish and chips!

There was access to a nice beach from the cabin and several other beaches and a nature walk within a short drive. I wouldn’t stay here again only because it was shockingly expensive. There’s great campgrounds nearby.

reviews.author: Deborah S.
reviews.text:
Campsites very nice. Campground quiet.
Restrooms desperate for upgrades. Campground host helpful.

reviews.author: Rachel O.
reviews.text: Kalaloch is a great spot for R&R on the coast. It’s peaceful and also close to nearby sights. Site B-11 was great — roomy, private, and located near the restroom and path down to the beach.

reviews.author: Piper C.
reviews.text: Great spot

reviews.author: Jack P.
reviews.text: Park was clean and very quiet.  Excellent trip

reviews.author: Art P.
reviews.text: Beach front campsites are different from forested campsites. Was confused by not being able to park car in the designated site. Otherwise the experience was very positive.

reviews.author: Patricia  K.
reviews.text:
this is an excellent location to explore the penisula side of olympic national park.
 very dog friendly as your dogs are allowed to be on the miles and miles of beach below the campground as long a they are on leash.   
the reason for the for the 4 vs. 5 stars is the D loop section we were on is directly behind highway 101 so it is very noisy.  Also our site # 20 was a pull through which is normally great but this one has  your rv door opening up to the busy road.  And there is no privacy behind you and the next site on the other side.   I would choose a different spot for sure, otherwise it was great

reviews.author: Rochelle  J.
reviews.text: Nice location within walking distance to the beach.

reviews.author: Amy  S.
reviews.text: Great campground, good facilities, great access to the beach too. We loved it and would recommend

reviews.author: Carenna W.
reviews.text: Clean campsite! Lucked out to get a spot right by the beach. We arrived around 8pm, and there were some open spots listed at the ranger station.

reviews.author: Shiena C.
reviews.text:
I went camping here with my boyfriend and we both really enjoyed this spot. We love how the shrubs gave us a privacy wall from people driving/walking by. The branches and shrubs were maintained allowing us to view the ocean and have enough leg room to set up our 10x8 tent and 10x10 canopy. 

The view of the ocean was beautiful and the sound of the waves was very relaxing at night. We did notice a couple small snakes near the shrubs closest to the road, but the snakes didn’t bother us. Surprisingly, there weren’t that many bugs around us. 

The stairs to the beach was only a 2 minute walk down which was very convenient for us. The walk to the restroom was less than a minute. There’s also a fish washing station, water pump, and the dumpsters near the restroom closest to the entrance of the campgrounds. 

We would definitely come back! Seeing the tree of life was nice as well.

reviews.author: Bonnie C.
reviews.text: Great time.  Clean.

reviews.author: Mary K.
reviews.text:
2024 was bad rain, rain, rain, we did not stay but we got a refund. We have been going to kalaloch since 1964. 
3 stars because it’s getting to hard for everyone to get a camp site.

reviews.author: Robert P.
reviews.text: Kalaloch is a very nice place. Campsites are clean and restrooms are in good condition. Given that the beach is only accessible from the campground, there’s never huge crowds. Can’t beat the sunset on a clear day.

reviews.author: Lauren Y.
reviews.text: We stayed at D37.  Definitely one of the nicest campsites in the entire campground!  The photos don't look that great, but it is definitely one of the roomier and more private sites, and there is a little trail through the vegetation that leads to a perfect spot for 2 small camp chairs perched on the cliff overlooking the beach.

reviews.author: Erin K.
reviews.text: A lot of the campground is right off the highway. There is quite a bit of road noise. However it is very beautiful and our site was huge. No soap in bathrooms and no showers. Had to walk to a dumping station to get our water.

reviews.author: Melaina B.
reviews.text: Stayed here for the proximity to the Hoh Rainforest and the ocean. It was so wonderful hearing the ocean waves at night. Had a great time tent camping here.

reviews.author: azmath s.
reviews.text: Loved everything about this campground. Ranger talk was fun and in the night we were very lucky to have a clear sky and we could see the Milky Way. Easily one of the best experiences in my life

reviews.author: Neil P.
reviews.text: Very nice location, beach and campsites. However, the restrooms were unpleasant and had some broken sinks and toilets.

reviews.author: Clarissa  F.
reviews.text: Was a great place with clean toilets and awesome view. The beach was very nice too

reviews.author: Elizabeth  C.
reviews.text: An awesome experience. The campsite was pretty and had a view of the water. Easy access to the beach and lovely walks in both directions.

The campground is nice because of it's proximity to the beach and tree of life, but I didn't have the best stay. Site D16 was very close to the road and their was car traffic noise the whole night. Once it was dark, our neighbors at the campsite across from us set up a big light on their camper and started playing a bocce ball game that involved throwing plastic balls on the paved road over and over again -- it was loud and annoying, especially since they only started after dark when there was not much to do except go to bed (since campfires weren't allowed). 

I would also like to request that the campground add soap dispensers to the bathrooms. The bathrooms were otherwise nice.

reviews.author: Jochen G.
reviews.text: Fantastic campsite, close to the beach under amazing trees formed by the ocean

reviews.author: John W.
reviews.text: Been going to Kalaloch Campground since the 1950’s. Now kids and Grandkids love it too. So upset done spaces are victim to erosion. Wish you could do something to prevent it! This place is so unique and lovely! Right on ocean which is rare for our State. Wish it was easier to get reservations! It’s a free for all! New staggered reservation makes it worse as more people are going after A and B loops in February instead of all park loops available. Go back to original. Please save this Campground from the Sea. Nothing wrong with saving it. Get out of Hippy mentality that Mother Earth is in charge as one Ranger told me 2 years ago!

reviews.author: Vincenzo L.
reviews.text: The campground is nice but this specific campsite is directly next to the main road. Make sure to bring esrplugs if you want to sleep well!

reviews.author: Nicole P.
reviews.text: This is one of the furthest campgrounds from most hikes and sites at this park - keep that in mind! But the beach is breathtaking,, the tidepools are awesome, and no matter what campsite you get, you will always hear the waves crashing at night - lovely. The only downsides to this stay (not counting the inevitable, incessant rain) was that there was no soap in the women's restroom for the entirety of my trip. Know ahead of time that you probably won't have service

reviews.author: Jessica C.
reviews.text: Campground was great. Plenty of bathrooms and beach access. There were day of cancelations so we were able to stay another night at a different site at the camp and enjoyed it

reviews.author: Rian G.
reviews.text: Beautiful camping spot couldn’t be better. Tree was close to camper but could back in ok. Might be harder to higher camper. Would love some showers…

reviews.author: Don I.
reviews.text: Campsite and picnic table floods when it rains,a lot of traffic noise on from hwy 101

reviews.author: Kimberly M.
reviews.text: I loved the view from my van of the ocean. It was a rainy stay but still well worth it. The bathroom was warm & clean which was a nice surprise. I’m looking forward to another visit.

reviews.author: Marissa m.
reviews.text:
despite the difficulty in getting a reservation the mere second when the website opened, it was worth the week of trying. 

It would be nice if a rinse station was  closer to the beach access.

reviews.author: Krista J.
reviews.text: Beautiful campground and beach.  Campfire ban during pouring rain was a bummer but I get it.

reviews.author: Lee B.
reviews.text:
PROS
* Check-in was easy.
* Facilities were close by and cleaned daily
* Sites are well spaced out
* Vehicle is not covered by trees so you don't have to worry about constant dripping from the trees after rain

CONS
* Site F004 is NOT for tent camping. Not enough level ground to set up a tent. 
* We had a roof top tent which was also a bit tight when folded out. 
* It also rained most of the time we were there and water does pool up on site (although does dissipate soon after it stops raining).
* No T-Mobile coverage on site (assuming because of trees) but if you go down to the beach you'll get 2 bars

reviews.author: Missy V.
reviews.text: We loved our stay at Kalaloch! Our camp site was spacious and it was a short walk to the beach. There was a bit of a walk to the bathroom though. And the closest bathroom did not have a water faucet so that made it a challenge to refill our water jugs. It would be so nice to add showers. I’d  be willing to pay extra per night to have showers added. My only other complaint is that the highway noise on 101 can get loud at night if you’re camped close. I really hope they think about expanding the campground in the future. It’s so competitive to get a spot! But we’re glad we were able to. Otherwise amazing beach and camp ground! I can’t wait to go back!

reviews.author: Maria G.
reviews.text: Nice site, amazing campground overall. No showers. If you're in a tent in heavy rain the tent spot itself does get flooded.

reviews.author: Mackenzie R.
reviews.text: We loved this campsite. Perfect location, beautiful beach, Tree of Life was sick, nice washroom facilities, bonus points for having electricity in washrooms.

reviews.author: Regina C.
reviews.text: This site was very private and quiet with a wide parking area and large area for tent(s).

reviews.author: MATRI L.
reviews.text: This is a very special spot! The beach is beautiful and the campground is very quiet, except for some noise from 101 for campsites closer to the road.

reviews.author: Rachel M.
reviews.text: Read the description of this site before booking! I did that and it was exactly what I wanted, but I had neighbors in a similar spot that were surprised. This is a small site with no privacy and no tent pad. That was just fine for me as I was camping in my car and was by myself so I didn't need a lot of space. I wanted this spot for the ocean view and it did not disappoint!

reviews.author: Anna L.
reviews.text: The site was awesome on the cliff looking at the beach. The only drawback was the fire ban, which we adhered to, but saw many people disregard…maybe better enforcement at night?

reviews.author: Daniel  K.
reviews.text: Great campground!! But D38 is too small, and ground is not leveled for one tent, nevertheless two tents. Book another site!

reviews.author: Diane W.
reviews.text: We loved our 1-night stay at Kalaloch Site D-36!  Nice level pad for our RV/van, with plenty of room behind the van to setup chairs to enjoy the ocean view and do some scent practice with the dogs.  We loved seeing the ocean out the back and side windows of our RV too.  It was worth practicing on the reservation system and being ready to select this site at 7 am PT.

reviews.author: Cylinda V.
reviews.text: Since camping sites vary in size, terrain, and noise level of Highway 101, the website provides excellent detailed descriptions to assist you in selecting the site most suitable.

reviews.author: Linda E.
reviews.text: Lovely spot and love the privacy- wish it was easier to get a spot!

reviews.author: Andrew N.
reviews.text:
When we booked the site we read the reviews…we did I promise!!! 

The road noise!!!! Wow…the road noise was a bit much. Not just a little!!! It sounded like these logging trucks were trying to make the most noise possible!!

The bathrooms smelled of urine and from a post from 2-3 months ago that someone else posted on is that the women’s bathroom is STILL not repaired!!!! One toliet not working!!! I asked of how often the bathrooms are cleaned and was told twice a day!!! Lies lies lies!!!!

Oh and don’t bring in firewood!!! Even if you don’t burn it in a fire ban, they’ll confiscate it!!!! People are having fires down the road for crying out loud!!!

Oh NPS…and vlolunters…do better!!! I mean what else do you have to do on a day to day bases!!!!

reviews.author: Sara P.
reviews.text: This was an amazing site next to the water, but I didn't read carefully and found out just before we left that it's a NO tent site. We were able to fit one small tent next to the firepit, but make sure to read the details of the space. Sites are very close to one another. Everything else was great! A short walk down to the beach and the perfect location to visit any of the Kalaloch beaches and Ruby Beach. Ranger Programs were awesome and we would definitely return again.

reviews.author: Kanako I.
reviews.text: Good location near the tree of life.

reviews.author: Sachin A.
reviews.text:
This campsite and location itself is magical

The toilets are disappointingly bad, inadequate management

reviews.author: Frank K.
reviews.text:
First off, majorly difficult to find your space , we were in a C loop, and no markings for how to get to the C loop, you have to go to a different loop, and eventually the road will come to the C loop. 
Next, our campground was right next to another space, too close for comfort. We decided not to stay.

reviews.author: Peter G.
reviews.text: What a treat to be able to stay at a campsite on the Olympic Coast! For most of our 7-night stay, we had ocean views on the A loop. Beautiful! We've stayed at Kalaloch several times before and the only constructive feedback we can give is that the bathrooms on the south side of the campground need updating desparately. The sink in the mens' in one of the bathrooms was out of commission our entire stay. The bathroom on the north side of the campground was newly-built.

reviews.author: Emery M.
reviews.text:
Please fix the showers/ add at least one set of shower rooms.

The experience at the campsite was great, the atmosphere of being in the forest next to the ocean is unreal. The campsite was clean, quiet, and every campsite seemed great. I wish there were showers though, we had to drive nearly 30 miles to get to some operating showers!

reviews.author: Melany  S.
reviews.text: Amazing campsite. Really clean and rangers/hosts frequent the campsite. Our neighbors had an off-leash dog and they noticed and asked for them to leash since we also traveled with our dog. Really close to the beach, spacious sites, and clean bathrooms. Really close to the tree of life.

reviews.author: Cynthia T.
reviews.text:
There was not any water available on the whole north end of the campground(loops D E F) except at the dump station. There used to be water spigots at each restroom and they have all been removed. 
Also, the reservation system has not improved over the past several years with the new staggered site reservations. There was still the issue of multiple empty sites even though it was super difficult and frustrating to get a couple of sites near each other, and the camp ground was supposedly “full”.
This was my family’s 34th year of camping at Kalaloch and by far the most difficult to secure sites and to then arrive and have half the camp ground empty was super irritating.

reviews.author: Oliver L.
reviews.text: Nice location, poor restrooms. Quiet.

reviews.author: Craig M.
reviews.text: We enjoyed our 2 nights in Kalaloch.   I give it 4 stars because of the dated facilities.   The camp hosts did a good job keeping them clean.

reviews.author: Jon F.
reviews.text: Generally a nice location. Some campsites backup directly onto US Hwy 101 and can be noisy. Great access to the beach at designated areas. Restrooms are small and not always clean.

reviews.author: Leah C.
reviews.text: Nice location. The bathrooms at Kalaloch are not as nice as some other campgrounds. Some cell service though!

reviews.author: Cuyler C.
reviews.text: Having a campsite overlooking the Pacific is incredible! The waves are the perfect white noise to fall asleep to.

reviews.author: Susan G.
reviews.text: Campsite unlevel, narrow roads, campsites very close.

reviews.author: KRISTIN M.
reviews.text: It was fine but campground a bit overrated imho.

reviews.author: Harriet W.
reviews.text: Beautiful campground on the beach.

reviews.author: Kelly B.
reviews.text:
This campsite is very small which we knew ahead of time but it rained constantly and a huge puddle ran underneath our canopy so we didn’t have a dry place to go. 

Plus the inconsiderate RV people across from us who didn’t want to smoke in their RV smoked on the road  so we couldn’t avoid smelling them every 10 minutes and if they weren’t smoking they were running their generator that smelled like exhaust and made its us super dizzy and sick. 

You probably won’t have neighbors like that but you won’t be able to avoid your neighbors in a site this small is the point of the story. 

Because there were no fires allowed we were able to set up a four person tent and a two person tent plus our 10 x 10 canopy to give you an idea of the size. 

Don’t recommend if it’s raining if your tent camping, but if you car camp it’s fine. 

Parking fit our standard minivan, but wouldn’t fit anything bigger.

reviews.author: Aleksandra  F.
reviews.text: It was an excellent weekend. The tent area on the roof is suitable for two tents (3-4 people) and offers good privacy.

reviews.author: Tanya C.
reviews.text:
Beautiful and clean campground, lovely host. I just wished there was a dish washing area nearer to loop D/E/F.  Difficult to tent camp otherwise. We had to carry our dirty dishes home. Also, the washrooms seemed always full and weren't the cleanest.

Also this campsite is really small, compared to the neighboring ones. The highway noise can be startling at night.

reviews.author: Arielle G.
reviews.text: Wonderful location! You can walk to several beach entrances and hear the waves from the campsites! Some campsites have beach views, which would be awesome. We saw sea otters and banana slugs - so cool. Plan ahead for it to be windy and cold though! Also, since it is such a beautiful campsite, it is super busy. Campsites are close together and there were several camping groups there that were loud past midnight. Still highly recommend due to the amazing nature views.

reviews.author: Veronica S.
reviews.text: I really liked this camping site. It's located right next to a trail that leads to the ocean. There's not much privacy since the spots are close to each other. However, the restrooms are clean.

reviews.author: Judith A.
reviews.text: The campsite and overall experience was, as usual, wonderful. We enjoyed time at Kalaloch, Beach 4 and even took a drive around Lk Quinalt.

reviews.author: Paul S.
reviews.text:
Please install showers, and somehow reinforce the campsites on the cliff with the ocean views, it is terrible to loose them to erosion.
Also, if not too impacting trails through the forest to the other beaches would be nice.  I am concerned about the environmental effects however and I do not know park policy. And get the people off of the tree of life, how disrespectful.

reviews.author: Halie G.
reviews.text: Amazing as always.

reviews.author: Marlen K.
reviews.text: Bathroom seems to be old with no soap and regular cleaning. Dump station came with a fee (in none of the other campgrounds in 9 different National Parks there has been a fee) although water to clean out grey water hose was not available.

reviews.author: altaf m.
reviews.text: Kalaloch campground is conveniently located in east part of Olympic with easy excess to the beach, bathrooms were average one of the sink faucet was broken, there is a potable water fill up and nearby hiking trail as well as easy access to other attraction, Olympic NP is huge so we split our stay at two location s starting at Kalaloch then driving Westward. It is a rain forest so plan a stay accordingly as you will get wet

reviews.author: lori s.
reviews.text: Concern so many sites reserved yet sitting empty

reviews.author: Michael L.
reviews.text: Kaloloch was excellent!  The views and beach cannot be diminished!!!

reviews.author: Salvatore M.
reviews.text: It was okay

reviews.author: Jessica W.
reviews.text: Such a beautiful, ethereal location. The beach is stunning, the campground simple but well kept and spacious. Perfect for tent camping. Some highway noise but mostly drowned out by the ocean; great for lovers of white noise. I would caution to keep a close eye on children if bringing them; the campground is perched on a small but steep cliff and there is plenty of access to the ledge. Beach access is via somewhat steep and uneven stones, stairs, and logs and it is important to watch the timing of the tides because the water comes up the side of the cliff at high tide and tosses the felled trees about like twigs. Beautiful to watch but dangerous to be trapped in the water with. Not to scare anyone away; this is an absolute stunner of a camping experience; just be mindful (especially with kiddos.)

reviews.author: Daniel H.
reviews.text: Overall we had a good experience but the men's bathroom sink was out of order and had a trash bag over it

reviews.author: rebecca t.
reviews.text:
This is one of the most competitive sites I've dealt with. Luckily there are many, amazingly I was able to reserve one beachfront after 2 years. You can still see the distant ocean from many others that aren't beachfront. 

We tried to get the same location two nights in a row. The folks who got one night arrived at 10 pm, set up half a tent, got drunk, slept in their car, and then left before 8am. It was a beachfront spot. People can camp respectfully on forest service roads nearby if they need a place to rest for the night and see the forest. If you're reserving a beachfront campsite for it's parking space, think about leaving it for a family who will be on ocean all day, watching their kids surf, or who will be exploring and appreciating Kalaloch for the gem that it is. Maybe those folks will come back sometime and really get to enjoy Kalaloch.

The staff was wonderful, the provided wood was pretty rough and full of knots, bring a big axe to use it, and the sites were clean. Awesome to have a merch nearby. Wish we could have been there longer. Please don't wash off sand in the bathrooms-- there are signs, but some people did it anyway and it clogs the sinks for everyone else and the hosts to fix. Get a bucket of water and rinse off outside. Bathrooms were getting new roofs which was great, they are taken care of and it's obvious that keeping this campground moving forward is a priority. 

Check out the beach at low tide, walk all the way to each end. Tons of waterfalls, eagles, even a seal. Watch out for waves. Some cool things washed up from China and Japan. Remember to take a handful of plastic back from the beach. Kalaloch is nice with it's dumpsters at the front. Check out the Really Big Tree off the highway to the north. Seems like an underrated spot to see the oldest cedar that exists on the whole planet. Steep gravel road, saw some dirt bikers up that way. Beautiful wildflowers. 
Kalaloch is within driving distance to Olympic for the day as well.

reviews.author: rebecca t.
reviews.text: Very beautiful campground! Don't wash off sand in the sinks and please take back any trash from the beach. The beach is a wonderful place to enjoy and explore any time, especially the rocks at low tide.

reviews.author: Diane L.
reviews.text: This is a beautiful area and the campground provided easy access to all the area beaches. Campground was well maintained and managed. Enjoyed our stay immensely.

reviews.author: Christina L.
reviews.text: Really enjoyed hearing the ocean as we fell asleep

reviews.author: Man N.
reviews.text: Beautiful campground.  Old and run down restroom.  Easy access to the beach.  I don't like the side parking but the camp itself was clean, flat, and usable.  Would stay again.

reviews.author: Leah S.
reviews.text: Camp host was friendly and helpful. Site was well maintained. Restrooms were clean.

reviews.author: Alexander S.
reviews.text: Thoroughly enjoyed my stay at Kalaloch Beach. Can't wait to come back again and explore the area further!

reviews.author: Bill w.
reviews.text:
We were in spot F25.  We were hoping to get #24 but it was under construction.  We also tried for #36 in the same loop.  After getting there and investigating the whole area, we had the most perfect spot of all.  We backed in.  Our view from that spot was unbelievable.  We could see the ocean from every window.  Even when it rained we could still enjoy it's magnificence .
This was our second time of being at Kalaloch.  It definitely won't be our last.
We have heard that the whole campground might be moved back on the other side of the highway.  
We think that is a lousy idea.  Even with the erosion please keep the ones that are still safe.  The front row views can't be replaced or beat.

reviews.author: Ryan M.
reviews.text: Such a cool spot with the ferns and mossy trees at the sites and then a quick walk onto coastline!  Great little family friendly trail next to campsite!  Loved exploring the the tide pools at nearby beaches as well.  The site was well maintained.

reviews.author: Tyler G.
reviews.text:
Site D39 was wonderful. Can see the ocean past the trees. We had just enough space for two small tents and there's a perfect spot for a hammock. Beware rodents. We had a mouse walk around our site during dinner and while we cooked smores over the fire. Crows were also quick to swoop in if anything was left unattended for more than a minute or so. Bathrooms were dated but clean. No hand soap, so bring your own. Small selection of overpriced groceries available at Kalaloch Lodge. Had to park kind in a very small parking pad in front of the site (kinda felt like we were in the road). 
Beach and Tree of Life was a very short walk down some stairs. 
Highly recommend Kalaloch campground nothing beats going to sleep to the sound of ocean waves (altough, you're likely to wake up to everything covered in droplets of ocean mist/dew). 
Near the Hoh Rainforest. 
Near and lots of other beaches (Ruby beach only 10 minutes away was lovely at sunset. Recommend Beach 4 at low tide for tide pools).

reviews.author: Beth L.
reviews.text: Great place - be sure to catch the rocks at low tide to see starfish!

reviews.author: Jeff H.
reviews.text: Very helpful camp host.  Nice site.  Easy walk to beach and to the Lodge

reviews.author: Anzhelika V.
reviews.text: Great place! We love it! Second time we stayed at the same lot) Beach and hikes are amazing!

reviews.author: Elizabeth M.
reviews.text: Campsites are packed in but the vegetation between sites felt really nice and made it more private feeling. Some road noise but not bad. Great access to the beach! Bathrooms on our end were so-so. The ones on D loop were so nice in comparison! Great access to Hoh Rainforest—be there by 9am.

reviews.author: Joy B.
reviews.text: Campsite was very small, and of course wet. Bathrooms were very dirty. The tree of life is great. We saw otters from the ledge!

reviews.author: Juliet A.
reviews.text: My husband and I stayed here in our camper van and the views were amazing if you have a rooftop tent! Only downside is the bathroom is a little far from site, so it wasn’t the best in the morning. Otherwise I highly recommend it.

reviews.author: David C.
reviews.text: Amazing camp site. The bathrooms are being updated but that’s a good thing in the long run. Well worth it!!

reviews.author: Asad R.
reviews.text: Amazing location, hard to book, bathrooms need to be reworked, no soap.

reviews.author: Anthony R.
reviews.text: Campsites go fast, especially if you have an RV over 25 ft... there is overflow parking available so it makes it nice if you have some family that is going to tent camp being in the same site as those in an RV.. only 1 vehicle typically fits per site, so the overflow is a bonus. Since there are about 7 different beaches you can explore, spending several days is ideal, although there is not any hookups so you have to be prepared... i use extra batteries and have a system to refill water.. you can fill your RV with water after you arrive so you don't need to haul water with you.

reviews.author: Maria C.
reviews.text: Stunning campsite, friendly rangers, short walk to store and lodge, one of a kind pristine beach access. One of our favorites!

reviews.author: Bryan C.
reviews.text: Beautiful

reviews.author: Vishnu P.
reviews.text: We like this great location and closeness to beautiful beach. This particular site is the smallest site location i have ever to.

reviews.author: Christine Z.
reviews.text: Very pleasant visit. Bathrooms were clean and spread out well.

reviews.author: Anne C.
reviews.text: This was a beautiful and well maintained park. We had a wonderful time and would go again. Our site was level and large, with no close neighbors. We didn't have a view of the lake but enjoyed walking down the trails to spend time at the beach. The shower would not go off when I finished, so it wasted a huge amount of water. I reported it and was told this was a known problem. There was some noise from the highway above us.

reviews.author: Yumiko M.
reviews.text: Beach side, huge camp ground. So many campers, but it was not too loud.

reviews.author: Halie G.
reviews.text: Went to beach 4 for the low tide to find tide pool and went to the tree of life. Recommend watching the sunset too

reviews.author: John W.
reviews.text: Site A30 is a great site that is big enough for a large tent. It is also just across from the beach trail. There’s plenty of room between A30 and other near sites. The restroom is close but not too close. Watching the sun set after 9pm and the rays of light coming through the trees was nice. There’s a convenience store 6 miles south in Queets that had gas, ice, firewood, etc.

reviews.author: Alexandra F.
reviews.text: Good campsite close to the beach trail and bathrooms. A bit exposed to the campsite it backed up to, but overall a great spot.

reviews.author: Laurie M.
reviews.text: The beach and tide pools were fun

reviews.author: Debra B.
reviews.text: Incredible views easy access to the beach campsite clean.

reviews.author: Kathleen R.
reviews.text: The campsite was big enough for trailer and vehicle. But we were disappointed that there was no water available in D, E or F. To get water we had to drive to the other side of the campground. We stopped at section A. I went into the ladies restroom. It was disgusting and only one stall available. The restrooms in our Section E was maintained.

reviews.author: Robert M.
reviews.text: Kalaloch is a magical world away from the daily grind. Such magnificent scenery. Such a wonderful getaway.

reviews.author: Elisa R.
reviews.text:
We loved our stay! A family of five, three kids (13m, 3years, 5years). We stayed at campsite D002 which was a dream! Really spacious, lots of trees around for the kids to play, the bathroom a short walk away, access to the beach after crossing the parking lot. We spend a lot of time simply on the campsite because our kiddos had so much fun playing between the trees and sitting around the campfire, and also down at the beach, the Tree of Life is right there! Lots of big log trees on the beach for climbing, the beach is sandy so sand castles were a must. The next day we drove to Hoh Rainforest which was about an hour drive, where we did the Spruce Nature Trail (1.2miles) which was so beautiful and easy enough for the kids. Make sure to ask for the Ocean steward and Junior Ranger programs at the Ranger station, if you complete it you get a badge which is just such a special and cool souvenir! On the way back we stopped at Beach 4. Make sure to check the tide schedule to come during low tide to see some beautiful tide pools. Getting on the beach is a little tricky (for kids)as the access point to the beach is a big rock which you can either climb down on a rope or navigate your way down the rock. It’s not hard hard but something to keep in mind. 
I cannot wait be back!

reviews.author: Naomi  R.
reviews.text: Nice campground. Sites mostly in woods but next to the beach

reviews.author: Ralph H.
reviews.text: Yearly family tradition.

reviews.author: amanda r.
reviews.text: we absolutely loved this campground!! the bathrooms were some of the cleanest i’ve seen at campgrounds i’ve been to. it was amazing to be staying just steps from the tree of life (must see) and the beach was so beautiful. we stayed in the D loop at site 34 and it was perfect. it is set back from the bluff but you can still see the ocean from it, much less windy than the sites right on the bluff and felt spaced out enough from the neighbors to have a little privacy.

reviews.author: Robert P.
reviews.text: Great campground with excellent beach

reviews.author: Tanner A.
reviews.text: Great spot at the end of the loop, honestly probably one of the best sites here. You get the ocean view from your tent without the wind of being on one of the bluff sites. It was my wife and I's first time back since I was a kid and the erosion has gotten pretty bad, the tree of life is about ready to fall so please don’t climb on it. Water/bathrooms/trash are a 1 minute walk from this site so that’s a plus. There’s no reason to buy firewood, they actually encourage you to use drift wood. And usually no soap in bathroom, no showers but the oceans right there. 10/10 already booked for next summer

reviews.author: Josh W.
reviews.text: Beautiful campsite along the ocean shore

reviews.author: Randy G.
reviews.text: This is a great campground, I’ve camped here since 1954! I’m aware of the pressure of so much usage. The National parks are doing what they can with a limited budget!  I’m not sure how the reservations system can be fixed but there should be a more severe penalty for not canceling reservations?

reviews.author: Christine  E.
reviews.text: Kalaloch is beautiful. There are trails, endless long beachwalks, the campsites feel pretty private (although the sites near Hgwy101 are subject to the occasional sound of trucks passing). I haven’t been to all of the parks in Washington, but this one is a standout. The rangers were very helpful and even tempered. We will be back.

reviews.author: Maura K.
reviews.text:
Absolutely spectacular site, with amazing sunset views and the crashing sound of the ocean to lull you to sleep at night.  Bathrooms left a lot to be desired in this loop...one toilet was out of water, and the other was far from clean and had a line.  But the direct Pacific Ocean views honestly made up for a LOT.

We fit a 21" camper van plus a 4-person tent on the site, and it was tight adding a car horizontally across the driveway opening.  The site immediately next to us was considerably bigger with a quite big "side yard."  No complaints, though.  I would joyfully have stayed here 2 weeks if I could have gotten the spots.

reviews.author: Janice E.
reviews.text:
We stayed three nights and really enjoyed our site. Most of the sites are very nice and all within easy walk to beach access. We lucked out with excellent weather. We did a day trip up to the Hoh River Rain Forest, and to Rialto Beach - lots to do in this region, including long walks on the beautiful beach right at the campground. 

I very much appreciated that there is a dump station at this campground ($10).

reviews.author: Gino G.
reviews.text: Site A25 has a super ocean view

reviews.author: Nicholas S.
reviews.text: Glorious as always.

reviews.author: Ross M.
reviews.text: Had a great time, interesting trees and surprising how quiet with so many campers. Just wish that the water in men's restroom worked but I aim to stay again in the future.

reviews.author: patrick r.
reviews.text: Beautiful location, campsite very good for tent camping, but bathrooms need an upgrade.

reviews.author: Robert W.
reviews.text: Have been camping at Kalaloch for decades. I love the lush rain forest environment and the sight, sound and smell of the ocean always excites and relaxes at the same time. Camp sites are nice and restrooms and water outlets are fine. This time I availed myself to the breakfast buffet served at the lodge and the price was very comfortable. Due to extreme drought conditions could not have a campfire this time but that may never have happened before; it is the rain forest after all.

reviews.author: Camilla C.
reviews.text: Great campsite location, close to beach access and short walk from toilets. No soap in the restrooms.

reviews.author: Nick S.
reviews.text: Site was clean and easy to find. No complaints.

reviews.author: Cameron P.
reviews.text: Great campground and site on the coast. Site 39 was laid out nice and the bushes provided privacy from other sites. Site was big enough for one 3 person tent & one 1 person tent. Site parking is parallel to the road. There is a private trail behind the site that leads to an overlook of the beach. Bathrooms were updated and very clean.

reviews.author: Kristin C.
reviews.text: We enjoyed our stay very much; our site was especially nice, away from the highway so we could listen to the ocean surf and a magnificent view a short walk away. The beach is fabulous, and we enjoyed beautiful weather. We also enjoyed walking through the rain forest nature trail.

reviews.author: Ethan M.
reviews.text: We had a great time. Our site in the campground C015 was great. Very large with space for two tents and protected in the woods so not too cold or windy.

reviews.author: Karen Alexandra M.
reviews.text: Nice spot for one tent and a car. Yes, it is by the Hwy so you would probably hear some cars. I love thia place so much I'm happy I got a spot. It was close to the path to go down the ocean, or also the path to go on a hike.

reviews.author: Joel P.
reviews.text: Beautiful location.

reviews.author: Dan B.
reviews.text: Hard to beat a campground on the beach, the views, the smells, the breeze. Try and grab a spot on the inside to avoid road noise, this place is fantastic!

reviews.author: Jesse W.
reviews.text: Fantastic campground! Perfect location with great beach access, nice bathrooms, and awesome scenery! D-39 was a good site with partial beach views, and pretty well isolated from other sites.

reviews.author: Brian C.
reviews.text: We were fortunate to get a mid-September reservation for this beach-front location in Kalaloch.  The campground is clean and quiet and the services are more than adequate.  Campsite RV pads are very tight, but the picnic table layouts are good and offer a modicum of usable area.  You'll be fairly close to your neighbors behind and beside you.  Erosion has closed a number of the very front sites, which actually provides more viewing space of the oceanfront for setback campsites.  Warm, layered clothes are recommended at this time of year and the prevailing incoming wind is fairly constant.

reviews.author: Konrad K.
reviews.text:
FirePit ohne Rost / grate!!!
Toiletten nicht nutzbar! Stark verschmutzt!
Self Check In!

reviews.author: Catherine C.
reviews.text: Beautiful setting, peaceful, spectacular. Spacious campsites. Convenient restrooms. And the icing on cake: bioluminescence in the waves at night! Truly magical.

reviews.author: Kristen W.
reviews.text: awesome campground. sites in the D group are right off the highway so lots of noise but there are plenty of sites at the facility that are tucked back and closer to the water.

reviews.author: Derwood S.
reviews.text: The beach was great especially for day break walks before others got out. Visit the rain forest a few miles north.

reviews.author: Dan C.
reviews.text: post-Labor Day weather was wonderful

reviews.author: Julianne  S.
reviews.text: This campground has wonderful ADA websites that are basically always reserved by non permit holders. the rangers do not care. ADA sites are on the reservation system and if any are first come first serve they are suggested by rangers to non permit holders. My partner is in a wheelchair and loves this campground, but unless we get lucky on the reservation system, an ADA site isn’t an option. Parking is tight in some spots. Rangers wouldn’t allow me to pass a reserved site to a family member driving to me and reserve a first come first serve for myself. The campground was full when they arrived. Rangers then asked us multiple times to rearrange our 2 cars so no tires were touching grass (2 were slightly off on one car) while other sites had vehicles fully on the grass. I wish the rangers had this same energy for preserving ADA sites for disabled members of the community.

reviews.author: Dorothy G.
reviews.text: This is a very beautiful place. Love the campground. The lodge has great services. Love the buffet breakfast there during the camping season. The view is breathtaking.

reviews.author: Michael T.
reviews.text: Great access to the beach.   Clean restrooms.   Store next to Kalaloch Lodge has all the basics that are needed and ice.   Also, they have great soft serve ice cream!   Close to Ruby Beach.

reviews.author: Margaret  C.
reviews.text: Nice campsite with good atmosphere and location, was super nice to be able to walk to the beach easily for sunset and hear the ocean at night. We also liked the location to get to the Hoh rainforest early in the morning. Campsites are very close together so no privacy from neighbors and the bathrooms (women’s specifically) are fine (flush toilets, running water) but rough shape.

reviews.author: Molly F.
reviews.text: A beautiful long beach, many lovely campsites, easy check in, and adequate bathrooms.  The store gets lots of use, so best not to rely on it, say for eggs!  There was some cell service for us there though.  And across the street there is a trail to the Forest Service Station.  It is safer than walking on the road....The station has info on hikes and the area in general.

reviews.author: Jacob G.
reviews.text: Beautiful place, definitely some road noise, but come on, we can't afford to put soap in the bathrooms???

reviews.author: Colin M.
reviews.text: What a wonderful campsite. As advertised, and the proximity to the beach is fantastic.

reviews.author: Katie A.
reviews.text: Great campsite along the Pacific Ocean with beautiful beaches and scenery. Multiple close hiking trails. Facilities were well maintained and staff was friendly. We will be back!

reviews.author: Kwanghoe M.
reviews.text: Beach is so beautiful

reviews.author: Joanna P.
reviews.text: Overall this campground is pretty awesome. How often can you stay somewhere with beach views for this price? The beach itself is wonderful, lots of smooth flat sand for long walks. The bathrooms needed to be cleaned/restocked more often for how many people were using them. Also, I ended up getting mice in my car here, but I'm not blaming the campground - just know that this is a flourishing ecosystem with all its critters! (And maybe try spraying around your engine with peppermint oil, which supposedly works to repel mice... I will be trying this from now on.)

reviews.author: Christopher G.
reviews.text: It was a great experience. Disappointed that we couldn’t have a campfire when it was Misty the whole time.

reviews.author: Dylan P.
reviews.text: The beach was wonderful and we could hear the waves from out tent. 10/10, I will definitely be returning.

reviews.author: Brandon B.
reviews.text:
It is a beautiful location. I love that the campsites are in the woods, but the beach is very close by. The tree of life was very interesting to see, as well as all of the drift wood structures on the beach. 
I recommend going to beach 4 at low tide to see the tide pools. Those were also incredible. 
Some of the campsite are close to the highway, which does have frequent road noise. and you might need to bring your own soap for the restrooms. Otherwise everything is great.

reviews.author: Patrick L.
reviews.text: Love this campground! Easy access to the beach, close to Ruby Beach and other beaches for tide pools. Some of the sites are a little small, and some lack much privacy from the sites around them, but it’s beautiful and I highly recommend it for camping with families especially.

reviews.author: Beth K.
reviews.text:
This campground is great. The access to the beach is easy no matter where you stay. The bathrooms are clean, and we’ll-maintained. The grounds were always cleaned up.

The site was not very private, but it wasn’t a problem. I would recommend this campground to anyone. The beach is beautiful, and there are lots of sand dollars to see!

reviews.author: Niall D.
reviews.text: Our family loves Kalaloch. We try to make it there every year!

reviews.author: Helmer K.
reviews.text: Beautiful campground with campsites overlooking the Pacific ocean. Restrooms are modern and clean but do not offer showers. You might think that the highway causes some noise pollution, however, the relaxing ocean sounds drown out any cars passing by.

reviews.author: Abraxaz S.
reviews.text: Coming from East Los Angeles, I wasn’t sure what to expect from Kalaloch. But my expectations were surpassed. This campground was so close to the beach, just a couple minutes walking distance. Not only that, but the restrooms were fairly close to my campsite, which was C002. The one thing that made me give 4 stars instead of 5 was that the campgrounds were fairly close to one another. I would have wanted some more privacy with my fiancé, especially with the lady adjacent from us who who had a dog that wouldn’t stop barking. All. Day. Long. And not only that, all we could hear he say was “BARKELY, STOP BARKING.” Maybe she shouldn’t have named her dog BARKley. So it was her dog barking and her barking as well. Other than that the Kalaloch campground was one I won’t forget about. It was very fun and a great memorable experience. I won’t ever forget it. Additionally I would like to add that the atmosphere here in Kalaloch is majestic. The lush trees and bright green atmosphere felt something out of a fairytale. No pictures, videos, or any online images with do this place justice. You just have to experience it for yourself. That being said… Kalaloch, until we meet again. ;)

reviews.author: nicole r.
reviews.text: a pretty small site but close to the bathroom and water spigot (a pro or con depending how you see it). the whole campground is close to 101 which is convenient but loud, especially with lots of logging trucks driving by at every hour. was a lovely location though otherwise and i recommend:)

reviews.author: Andy J.
reviews.text: My partner and I had an amazing trip at Kalaloch! We were so grateful to have out dog with us and to be able to bring her to the beach. The campsite felt so tucked away in the dense trees, so we didn't feel like we were just surrounded by campsites on all sides. The sink in the bathroom nearest to us wasn't working which was a bummer, but certainly not the end of the world. We had our sanitation products to keep ourselves relatively clean. We will definitely be returning here someday soon hopefully!

reviews.author: Ian L.
reviews.text: Site A025 was a great campsite with an ocean view and a little bit of shade as well. The path down to the beach was just a few campsites down. The beach itself is fantastic, soft sandy beach, great for kids to run around. Short walk to the tree of life. Highly recommend this campground and this site specifically.

reviews.author: Matthew C.
reviews.text: Beautiful quiet campground at night. Right at the beach and you can hear the waves breaking.

reviews.author: K Lee T.
reviews.text:
I visited with two different camp hosts, first night was Dan and second night was Chris - both were very friendly and helpful.  
The bathroom at the north entrance of B & C rows was not in very good condition. One of the two stalls was out of order, there was no hand soap and the hand dryer did not work. 
Many of the tent sites had concrete blocks preventing vehicles from angling into the site which made no sense. I have a tent that fits on the back hatch of my SUV and it cannot be used since the vehicle is blocked from the site. Why are the concrete blocks there? Example is site B1.

reviews.author: William B.
reviews.text: Very quiet, shady, beautiful campground with limited cellular service.

reviews.author: Craig B.
reviews.text: This is my favorite location and place I have visited for the past 60+ years. If I need to reset the mind and soul this is it.

reviews.author: John F.
reviews.text: Great beach location. Trees helped shelter us from rain. Miles of beach access for walking. Was a little close to the road.

reviews.author: Shelly M.
reviews.text: This site (A13) is one of the more spacious sites with an ocean view. The double driveway was able to fit two pickups plus my Aliner trailer. Sites vary greatly and I would not camp here in a site on the road- the log trucks are unbearable. 4 stars because the bathrooms are not good. The one closest to us was in disrepair with only one working stall so there was always a line. No soap (as usual) and the dryer didn’t work. There was no tp for a day and a half. Overall a beautiful campground and beach but camping is a bit rough due to weather (hope for sun), wind (comes with the view sites) and sand. Shout out to ranger Janet Jackson who got our friends a site last minute and took no bull from anybody.

reviews.author: Andrei G.
reviews.text: Nice place, ocean was louder than a US-101 nearby, so being next to the road wasn't an issue. Would be nice to have a shower on the campground.

reviews.author: Jenn V.
reviews.text: I absolutely love the location.  We had a site near a beach path that let to the ocean and spent hours and hours wading, picnicking, beachcombing and flying kites at the beach.  It was stunningly beautiful. We felt like one of nature's most beautiful playgrounds was in our backyard.  The only gigantic drawback was our campsite.  We were in a site that literally had no barrier (not even space) between us and our neighbors.  They could hear our conversations and we could hear theirs. Our picnic table were probably no more than 15 feet from theirs.  It was like we were sharing a single site.  It was hard to pretend that you didn't notice them. So my advice is to read the descriptions of the sites very carefully.  Some are very small (not accommodating to anything other than sleeping in your vehicle or a very small tent), some lack privacy and some back up right to highway 101 so the traffic noise is prominent and I think traffic may also even be visible.  Bathrooms are rudimentary -  aging, cold water only and no soap dispensers.  All that said, I would go back in a heartbeat because of the access to the beautiful locale.  I would just do a little better job vetting campsites next time.

reviews.author: Heather M.
reviews.text: This is a fantastic campground with great trees and shade for almost every site and incredible beach access.

reviews.author: Diana  M.
reviews.text: I loved the campground, very clean, quiet and organized. Our space was more than enough for our car and tent. I think it is small for an RV, but luckily that was not the case. The beach is beautiful, the spot we got was stunning in front of the beach. We had super close "The tree of life", 5 min walking. There is dump containers (bear proof), and accesible restrooms. The only missing thing (to me) was showers services.

reviews.author: Andrea G.
reviews.text: Campground was beautiful. However the site was located close to the road, so there was a good deal of traffic noise at this site.

reviews.author: Andrea G.
reviews.text: Campground was beautiful. Site had good privacy and was close to the beach side of the campground/beach access. Bathrooms were basic but clean.

reviews.author: Darrell C.
reviews.text: nice

reviews.author: Rachel  S.
reviews.text: Stayed in several campgrounds in ONP, this was my favorite. The privacy was pretty good because of plants/trees and the beach was lovely.

reviews.author: Kaila R.
reviews.text: This was our 30th summer of camping here. Absolutely love the place!

reviews.author: Richard R.
reviews.text: The campground is beautifully situated and well maintained. The campsites are a short walk from the beach, from which you can watch the sun set over the Pacific. We enjoyed a peaceful stay on the last day of a five day trip around the peninsula. It was a lovely way to end our trip.

reviews.author: Tom S.
reviews.text:
Overall a great place to visit. Unfortunately when we were there the mens bathroom near us had a broken sink to teeth brushing was a bit of a drag.
Beautiful beach that the kids swam in as the tide was coming in (to avoid rip currents) and easy access to Hoh Rainforest, the Big Cedar and other fun

reviews.author: Mikulas N.
reviews.text: Clean sites steps from the beach in a beautiful setting, no showers but enough facilities to stay for few nights.

reviews.author: Carolyn K.
reviews.text: Site C012 was conveniently placed near the bathrooms, yet tucked within the trees. The bathrooms were clean and the spot was quiet despite having nearby neighbors. Very beautiful site, and just a short walk from the beach. Be sure to check out the Tree of Life, and find some tide pools.

reviews.author: Daniel W.
reviews.text: Beautiful spot with easy access to the beach. The restrooms near my campsite left some to be desired. Would gladly stay again.

reviews.author: Joost d.
reviews.text: The campground is beautifully located in a rainforest next to the beach. There is lots of shade and enough privacy between sites. The one downside is that some of the sites are essentially next to the highway. There is not much traffic during the night, but it is not the most quiet location.

reviews.author: Aidan O.
reviews.text: Site E02 is a little cramped and not very flat, but it is relatively private and just steps from the bluff. It's also well-positioned between two restrooms. Every site has trade-offs now that the best sites are literally falling onto the beach, but E02 was an absolutely lovely place to spend a few nights. This was also the first time that I've had fairly regular cell and data service here, which may or may not be a plus for some people.

reviews.author: Ian J.
reviews.text: Fantastic, beachside campground with amazing views, clean bathrooms, and more.

reviews.author: Angela S.
reviews.text: My family has been coming to Kalaloch for 3 generations now and it never disappoints.

reviews.author: Janet W.
reviews.text: There were so many empty sites while we were there that went to waste when people were coming in looking for a site. Don’t like the two week ahead reservations. Prefer the 6 month reservations like before.

reviews.author: Norbert L.
reviews.text: Beautiful

reviews.author: Sarah B.
reviews.text: Wow! This is an amazing campground perched above Kalaloch Beach. Clean, friendly and helpful host. Would stay here again in a heartbeat! Great location to access beaches with tide pools, beautiful sunsets, and Hoh RainForest. Flat beach (depending on tides) also allows for great moonlit walks to watch the stars!

reviews.author: Michael M.
reviews.text: Please trim back the tree in loop A that is too low to accommodate RV’s. It damaged my camper and obviously has been struck numerous times by other vehicles.

reviews.author: Mike G.
reviews.text: Super excellent and very far out!

reviews.author: Lara H.
reviews.text: The forest is amazing and the beach is beautiful!  We always enjoy the walk up the beach to see the rocks and features at the north end of the beach.

reviews.author: Femke M.
reviews.text: Beautiful beach, beautiful campground!

reviews.author: Cathy R.
reviews.text: Good location. We were there to have a place to sleep for the night. Close to other sites, no privacy. The bathrooms and beach access were within a comfortable walking distance. Close to the highway, traffic noise is loud; ocean waves can be loud too. Tree of life is right there. Ruby Beach is 8 miles away, beaches 1-4 are very close. Thank you. Worth it if you can get it booked.

reviews.author: Susan K.
reviews.text: The BEST place to camp!! Kalaloch has many different beach trails, that are all unique. The lodge has fun dining. And the little store has all you need for a long stay.

reviews.author: Brian D.
reviews.text: Beautiful, large, private sites--many near the beach.  It was wonderful to fall asleep to the sound of the surf.  The only improvement I would suggest would be to upgrade the bathrooms, since they are old and dingy-looking.

reviews.author: Jo p.
reviews.text:
I have stayed or stopped by many of the National Parks over the years. The bathrooms at Kalaloch were DISGUSTING! There was no toilet paper in mid-afternoon, mornings, evenings, and throughout the day. The toilets, floors, and sinks were so dirty!!! When I went to the ranger station, no one was there multiple times throughout the day. I had to ask another camper to hand me toilet paper and they too were without. A child was crying at another time because they did not have toilet paper. My heart broke for the child. I ran to my own campsite to get a napkin for them (so humiliating). Other campers were also complaining and disappointed. 
Different subject, dogs barking (why would I leave home?).  Another subject, so many open campsites and it took me forever to get a campsite. It takes hours to get there and there more open campsites although they said reserved.  This system is NOT working. Kalaloch Campground deserves better attention. I could clean the restrooms and get the job done. This was NOT acceptable but still my favorite place to stay. I will bring my own toilet paper, bathroom cleaners, ear plugs, dry firewood (the wood at the lodge was too wet to burn), and... still beg for a spot!

reviews.author: Sue C.
reviews.text: Restrooms were very dirty. Lot is uneven and small, no shade!

reviews.author: Arnold W.
reviews.text: The weather was great. The beach is wonderful and our campsite was adequate. It would have been nice to have a little more privacy.

reviews.author: Allen H.
reviews.text:
Ok it rained! Added to the fun frankly. The facilities were first rate.  Beng so close the the ocean and the tree of life. Perfect. Plus if you want an espresso there’s a place about a mile down the road. 
Best spot to camp if visiting the Olympic National Park!

reviews.author: Serhii K.
reviews.text: Great location but minus 1 star for the condition of the restrooms. Some of them didn't work and they didn't even have a hand soap :/

reviews.author: Chad P.
reviews.text: Awesome beach. Very much enjoyed seeing the tide at different levels and running along the shore with the pup. Nice Park Rangers - certified the pup as a Bark Ranger and showed a presentation of some sort that we missed. General store within walking distance proved valuable when missing tin foil.

reviews.author: Rachel O.
reviews.text: B3 was a large site with a fair amount of privacy compared to others. It’s a short walk to the restroom. Be aware it’s near the fish cleaning station and there’s a power box near it that turns on and off a few times each night.  Campground is well kept and campers are good with the noise curfew.

reviews.author: Susan R.
reviews.text: Beautiful place. The only problem is some of the roads are one way and opposite of how you have to park your trailers. Makes it hard to get in your spots.

reviews.author: Edwyn A.
reviews.text: Ocean side location is pristine. Only a quick walk away from the tree of life

reviews.author: Matthew M.
reviews.text: Location to the beach is nice, campground is crowded and noisy.

reviews.author: Lynette D.
reviews.text: Kalaloch has a beautiful combination of forest and ocean.   We stayed in site A43 and it was spacious and private. I also appreciated it’s proximity to the restrooms. Restrooms were always clean and well stocked.  We attended the ranger lecture and found it entertaining and informative.  The park was surprisingly quiet given that it was almost full.  At night, we could hear the ocean from our site.  However, we could also hear the highway noise as we were not far from the road but it wasn’t constant. When we walked the campground, we were impressed with how unique each site was and the careful planning that was used in clearing the least trees possible.  We would definitely return.

reviews.author: Alexander P.
reviews.text: Premium location right in front of the beach (but not on the beach, therefore not as exposed). Well-located if you are interested in visiting the Quinault or the Hoh Rain Forest (or of course if you want to experience the beach). The other parts of the park (Sol Duc, Hurricane Ridge) are a bit far away (min 2 hour drive). The park is right next to the highway 101, try to get a campsite close to the beach to avoid the noise and get a nice view.

reviews.author: mercedes c.
reviews.text: I loved the campground and hike. The environment is perfect.

reviews.author: Laurie S.
reviews.text: Nice campground. Sites along the water are especially nice. Facilities are fine. Nice easy trail accessible from campground.

reviews.author: Mke I.
reviews.text: Enjoyed our stay, walk on the beach, visit up to Ruby Beach and Hikes in Hoe Rain Forest  Plan for long waits (2HR's) at Rain forest due to construction and small parking area.

reviews.author: Hemanga B.
reviews.text:
It's just next to the ocean. Perfect venue to unwind.

Only thing missing is a shower to clean up after getting wet at the beach.

reviews.author: Chelsi R.
reviews.text: The best campground you can book on the coast at the Olympic National Park.

reviews.author: Jim N.
reviews.text: We stayed in E012 it was a great space. Very large and would book again.

reviews.author: Daria  S.
reviews.text: Amazing campsite. Very peaceful, tucked neatly in the bushes and trees. Can’t see the water from it though.

reviews.author: Daria  S.
reviews.text: Beautiful campground. We enjoyed sunset walks on the beach. The campsite was small and not very private, and it was hard to put stakes in the ground, almost like the whole campsite had a layer of cement underneath the leaves and mulch.

reviews.author: Chelsea M.
reviews.text: The campground is kept very clean even the facilities on site. The access to the beach is super easy and close. The tree of life is actually right below loop D on the beach. It’s really quiet there as well. We will definitely be going back.

reviews.author: Sarah M.
reviews.text: Sites are really spacious & mostly pretty private. We backed up to the main road and traffic was definitely noisy in the evening and early AM. Bathroom facilities were mostly kept up but it is such a bummer not having any shower facilities since it’s a beach site. The sand + saltwater + more and more sand with young kids was definitely challenging. There is a foot wash station by bathrooms and that became our freezing cold showers. But having even just one full full size outdoor shower to rinse after a fun day on a beach would be a very welcomed game changer. However, the sunset views, privacy, and general lack of crowds/congestion still made it totally worth the stay.

reviews.author: Chris B.
reviews.text: We were fortunate to land a terrific site with a great view. I had no idea Washington had beaches like this and I’ll definitely be back!

reviews.author: Fred A.
reviews.text: We had reservations in the main campground, we arrived a couple days early so we stayed at southbeach, wonderful spot so we gave up our spot at the campground and stayed at south beach.  We did notice the campground was fully booked on line, when we drove thru the park was mostly vacant.  Not really happy with the new camping reservations.  The local customers that support the park year round can not get good spots unless you book a few days in advance, if you work you must plan ahead, that means most of the bookings are  not in the great spots.  Also way to many good spots were empty for days.  Maybe look into how the state and county parks run their reservation system.  We love Kalaloch and enjoy the off season to. Our stays are aways awesome.

reviews.author: Eric b.
reviews.text: No soap was a little weird but overall amazing camp ground.

reviews.author: Robert I.
reviews.text: Perfectly as advertised! You are definitely unplugged but still have the amenities needed for extra comfort. We took our 2 & 3 year olds with us and the canopy cover provided enough shade in the early evening to go to bed before the sun went down. Being steps from the beach was a huge perk! The mercantile shop just down the road was a great spot to pick up local firewood and a quick soft serve cone.

reviews.author: Joel  A.
reviews.text: We stayed at a very small spot next to the beach. People drove too fast and were distracted looking at the beach most of the time. I felt unsafe for my kids so I was on edge most of the time.

reviews.author: Pamela O.
reviews.text:
The campground is really nice and so close to the beach! The restrooms and water sources were spaced around the campground (sink in men's room wasn't working when we were there). When we were there (7/5-7/7) it was extremely quiet at night, which actually surprised us (in a good way). The beach is easy to walk on and Ruby Beach is a short drive away. Sunset was amazing.
The campground is pretty isolated, so come prepared with everything.

reviews.author: Maura C.
reviews.text: We loved this campsite. Our canopy has a privacy wall which worked perfectly and we were able to park our car for more privacy. We have a 8 person coleman tent which fit with no issues. Road noise did not bug us. Close to bathrooms. We weren't impressed with many of the sites because of privacy and their size. We would stay at A40 again!

reviews.author: Dana M.
reviews.text: We had a great site on a bluff overlooking the beach that was very private and quiet.  I did note that some of the sites were much smaller, and some were right on the highway with almost no shrubs/trees to block the highway view.  We were very happy with our experience but wouldn't want to stay in one of those sites!

reviews.author: Barbara C.
reviews.text: Beautiful experience for me! My campsite was spacious and allowed for my brother's family to tent with room for my RV. The younger boys had so much fun exploring the beaches and trails. I have limits on my mobility but was still able to easily view the beach from the trail top and even got down and back up the beach stairs once (with help). Although the camp ground was full, the beaches never seemed crowded and the Rangers and Hosts were always friendly and helpful. Loved that there were no vehicles racing up and down the beach. Relieved a lot of worry while the kids were playing in the sand.

reviews.author: Maxim S.
reviews.text: Great spot

reviews.author: Doo B.
reviews.text: The site A19 had a great location with tall shrubs making the site very private. It's very close to the beach 2 minute walk to the silky soft sand and waves. There's a picnic area on one side and an empty lot on the other. It had a large picnic table and a fire ring with a thick metal and a thin mash-type double grill. They were height adjustable too. The tent area was secluded by salmon berry bushes. The sound of the sea was constant and powerful 24/7 like camping next to a large waterfall! Overall, we enjoyed staying camping here.

reviews.author: sungho k.
reviews.text: It is a campground with beautiful scenery of the Pacific ocean. The restroom is clean and well maintained. Park rangers patrolled every morning.

reviews.author: Stephanie S.
reviews.text: The location is convenient, easy to get to beach and restrooms. The campground was clean, bathrooms too. The four stars come from the location, convenience, and general cleanliness.  The convenience and proximity to bathroom and beach trail is what makes this particular site. Be warned this particular site doesn’t have a good space for a tent a safe distance from the fire pit. Parking was tight for a Toyota Corolla. Spaces are close together. There is noise throughout the day, includes screams kiddos.  Quiet after everyone goes to sleep.

reviews.author: Elizabeth C.
reviews.text: The restroom situation was horrid. In my loop one stall and one sink in the women’s side, the other was out of order.

reviews.author: Courtney  G.
reviews.text: Campsites are what you expect. Not many have beach views but that was fine. Bathrooms were very poorly kept up. Men’s sinks were covered and unusable. Several broken down stalls, no soap anywhere. Very dirty and dilapidated.

reviews.author: June  B.
reviews.text: Beautiful camping!!! Beach is amazing and so close. Tree of Life is a must 💕

reviews.author: Yiling X.
reviews.text: Stunning view! Just a bit too windy during the daytime

reviews.author: John M.
reviews.text: The staff was very helpful with everything we needed to make a perfect stay!

reviews.author: elisabella t.
reviews.text: We got lucky with our spot, great space and I was able to reverse park my truck. The beach was beautiful!

reviews.author: James P.
reviews.text: Great blend of forest/beach/tide pools.  Quiet, comfy and convenient.

reviews.author: Iris G.
reviews.text:
Overall 8/10
Easy beach access, flushable toilets, running water, camp was very full, lots of dogs, enjoyed the driftwood structures on the beach

reviews.author: Bob  L.
reviews.text:
There is a tree branch right near spotA22 that tore off my roof rack, and it had been hit numerous times 
The ranger did nothing above it and said he couldn’t 
Ridiculous

reviews.author: garry g.

The next sites tent area does come close to the one at this site but in our case it was a non issue. The bathrooms are a short walk down the road and where not busy at all even with a full camp ground. reviews.author: Shirley L.
reviews.text:
This was a very good campground if you are seeking the more remote beaches of the Olympic National Park. I take it the northern part and its beaches are more popular. 

This has a step down into the Beach and is beautiful overall campsite. I did not feel the campsites were jammed right next to each other. It felt relatively private. The campsites however can be quite small. Bathrooms felt clean though a lot of moths. There were spigots for potable water. 

My particular site was somewhat small. It is surrounded by trees and had a tree stump when you stand you can see the ocean. The ground is rocky though so really hard to stake a tent in. It is much better suited to SUV camping.

reviews.author: Vera H.
reviews.text: Nice site, just s bit of sun. Close to restrooms (not that good) and beach access. A bit of sea view, if rhere is no RV. Difficult hanging a sleeping  mat.

reviews.author: Christine R.
reviews.text: Visited mid-June, Monday through Wednesday. Campground was relatively busy but not full. While the camp sites are small, it didn't feel like we were on top of our neighbors and it wasn't too loud. There is some road noise, but you can also hear the ocean waves. The campground bathrooms have flush toilets and running water, but no soap, so bring your own. The bathrooms were relatively clean, but sandy. There's also water spigots for washing dishes and dumpsters for trash/recycling. The Kalaloch beach is very nice, clean, and not too busy. The campground is close to many other beaches and the Hoh Rain Forest. If you don't want to eat at the Kalaloch Lodge, food is 40 minutes away in Forks or Quinault. Very limited cell reception, but the area is well marked and easy to navigate by road signs.

reviews.author: ayse s.
reviews.text: OMG! Beautiful Beach! Great campground! Bring your own soap for bathroom. I would definitely come back!

Plenty of space away from other sites; close to C017 which was where  our friends were camped. The space is open between the two sites so easy access and only 20' between firepits. Also site is located midway between two restrooms/water spigots/ garbage. Flush restrooms ok, plan to bring your own hand soap. Very quiet and respectful campers. Several ways to access the beach. Enjoyed Kalaloch Creek Nature Trail as well. Will return.
