reviews.author: Cassandra H.
reviews.text: Kalaloch is the best beach camping to be found! The views are spectacular.  We love hanging out where the creek meets the ocean for the day.  No hot water, hand soap, showers or cell service (spotty at best for Verizon). If you're looking to get away and relax, this is it!

reviews.author: Katrina  K.
reviews.text:
I was in space A003, which is one of the spaces listed as having road noise from the highway. It definitely does! Fortunately at night there aren’t a lot of drivers, so it quiets down, but definitely expect to hear cars all day in this space. 

Also in the A loop, the women’s restroom had two stalls, but one of them was out of order the entire weekend. This resulted in lines forming and was difficult for me and for some of the kids I saw around. 

Those were the biggest drawbacks. However, the up sides were numerous! You can walk down to Kalaloch beach from the campground (and my space next to the campground host was very close to the pathway). Kalaloch beach is quiet and flat. Kind of similar to Ocean Shores and Long Beach, but not very populated. 

Plus the AMAZING Ruby Beach with gorgeous sea stacks is a quick ten minute drive up the road and extremely worth a visit. I went down there three different times over a two-night stay. Just amazing. It was more popular, but because it’s so large and there are so many sea stacks, it didn’t feel crowded even on a sunny afternoon. When the tide was coming in at sunset, I was one of 5 people down there watching the breakers crash and a sea lion play in the waves. 

The campground itself was clean, and I appreciated the water station next to the restrooms. I’d definitely camp here again, but might try to get a spot further from the highway.

reviews.author: David W.
reviews.text: Kalaloch is a beautiful place to walk the beach and look at tidal pools during low tide.  There were three problems I noted during my recent stay.  The first and most serious was the terrible condition of the restrooms in the campground.  There was no soap.  There was filth, everywhere.  The smell was overpowering.  Granted, they need to be completely redone (the facilities are beyond repair) but still, they could have installed some soap dispensers and cleaned them once in a while.  The second problem was that Kalaloch suffers from what I call "Washington dog owner carelessness" and by that I mean well over half of the visitors to the place bring their dogs and many do not use leashes despite the requirement.  They're running amok on the beach and cause a distraction to what would otherwise be a great experience.  Finally, despite the clearly labeled "no campfires on the beach" signs, there were multiple groups with campfires on the beach, some of them quite large, and no visible enforcement of the rules.  Despite these shortcomings, we had a wonderful time and I'd encourage people to visit.  But...Kalaloch needs to know that they can improve, particularly by putting soap in restrooms.

reviews.author: Alexander S.
reviews.text:
These sites are somewhat small and compact, but they're clean and the area is very nice. Good bathroom facilities and water spigots.

Our site specifically (A008) had a broken grill on the fire-ring, which was inconvenient but ultimately we were able to make it work. The canopy protects pretty well from light rain, and overall the area is damp, so it stays nice and cool. Be sure however to bring kindling wood or a firestarter if you plan on burning wood. Additionally, consider having a good means to pound stakes into the ground, which was mostly embedded with lots of small gravel and dense earth.

The sites also have great access to the beach; our site was maybe 150ft from the beach entrance, and many of the sites even overlook the beach, which I would highly recommend if you can get them.

Finally, there were a lot of families and the campground seems very popular in the summertime, so if you're looking for a bit more privacy this isn't the best choice, however everyone was overall very polite and respected quiet hours and their neighbors well.

reviews.text:
Kalaloch has been a favorite campground since childhood. The geologic variation and scenery of the nearby beaches is what keeps me coming back, along with the beauty of the rainforest. Kalaloch beach has a smooth shallow contour making it perfect for skim boarding. 4th beach has tide pools and beautiful driftwood . Ruby beach offers haystacks (rock outcroppings), large drift logs, and a freshwater pool at the bottom of the creek. Third beach is steep but great sight seeing, fishing, and we saw whales spouting just off this beach in late July. Beaches south of Kalaloch have large flat stones. 
There are no showers offered at the campground. It is becoming excessively difficult to book campsites at Kalaloch because of popularity. Click fast, just as they open up for reservations six months in advance. Good Luck.

reviews.author: Sydney R.
reviews.text: Had so much fun, this trip was very memorable for our family. Our spot was clean, the bathrooms were also clean. The beach is beautiful. And we escaped the heat wave the rest of the state was experiencing. Our 9 month old doesn't like sleeping in the tent much. So we took a spot next to the highway. We were one of the few sleeping near the highway so we had much privacy. The spots are much closer to the highway than I imagined they would be. Maybe less than 50 feet, but not sure exactly. Ive slept near roads before but usually there is more footage between the site and road. You will get bright lights and hear loud trucks passing by. Thankfully those sounds did not wake our baby and the sounds of the waves were present and actually kept her asleep thru the night. Id probably do it again to avoid bothering my neighbors with a crying infant. The other downside was there were few water stations, and the closest to us was out of order, so we had to walk a long distance to get water.

reviews.author: Peter G.
reviews.text: Great campsite! I know it's tough to get a site here, but so worth it. Bathrooms were cleaned daily! Loved that the Host site had items that were found and could be borrowed, returned for others to use.

reviews.author: Mala A.
reviews.text:
Washrooms we’re not clean, no hand washing soap( Covid still exists and this being a national park?) Park host was now welcoming or friendly. 
It is a great location, excellent beach access and the sites are decent size and private.

reviews.author: Christopher E.
reviews.text: Sites were generously spaced, giving better privacy.  Some sites, including mine, are fairly close to US 101,  However, traffic slacked off significantly as the night progressed, and the sound of the ocean drowned out what little vehicle noise remained.  Very good national park campground.

reviews.author: Lauren  W.
reviews.text: If you are looking for peace and quiet…this definitely isn’t the place for you. People stay up and part my pretty late and it’s filled with playing children (which of course should be expected on weekends and summer time). It didn’t bother me in the least, but if you want quiet don’t come here lol. However, the beauty you will experience is so worth it. I was on a camp site closest to the freeway (must have been a last minute cancellation) but it was a nice size and it felt like being right in the forest yet just a short walk to the beach and to the tree of life which is a must see. I really hope to come back again!

reviews.author: Sarah B.
reviews.text: The location is wonderful and you hear the ocean at night. The campground is quiet. We were very close to the neighboring campers. The camp host was not around much and the bathrooms needed soap the whole time we were there and were not clean.

reviews.author: Tracey W.
reviews.text: Campsites close to the beach. The beaches  were beautiful! The bathrooms were sparse and only one sink so don’t plan on using the restroom to brush teeth or get ready for evening. They have water to rinse dishes etc which was nice.

reviews.author: Emily M.
reviews.text: Kalaloch is wonderful. My only complaint is that the bathrooms don't have soap.

reviews.author: Betty W.
reviews.text:
Being at the ocean has always been a special experience for me and brings back many memories.  I was fortunate enough to have one of the bluff cabins.  They are comfortable, not fancy but perfect for the place!
We loved the walk in the spuce burls at Beach 1 just 1 1/2 miles south of Kalaloch.  Also loved our hike down the beach to Browns Point.

reviews.author: Dawna D.
reviews.text: Beautiful location! The beach is fantastic!

reviews.author: Alex P.
reviews.text: A027 must be one of the best campsites here. Totally private. The ocean is so loud, you can't hear any other people. There's a big tree on the campsite, which you can climb for a great sunset view. The trail to the beach is just one campsite away to the south.

reviews.author: Emily D.
reviews.text: We love it here. You have large trees to help shade you and to explore around. The beach is just right there on the other side. Plenty of beach area and space for everyone . Highly highly recommend the ranger walk at the tide pools at beach 4. We found hundreds of sea creatures and the ranger was so friendly and knowledgeable

reviews.author: Joey A.
reviews.text: Unbelievable place. We loved it so much! I wish we stayed longer, but definitely will be back. Highly recommend!

reviews.author: Biljana  P.
reviews.text: Just amazing, the sound of the ocean and the birds.

reviews.author: Walter A.
reviews.text: Kalaloch is a personal favorite. This week I was blessed to have 4 nights oceanfront. This specific site could have had a bit better ocean view if The bushes were trimmed back a bit, but at the same time those bushes cut down the wind and were an excellent privacy divider with neighboring campsites. All the camp neighbors were respectful of quiet hours. Kalaloch’s weather is always a bit fickle, but we had sun every afternoon and incredible sunsets. We also like the convenience of the store at the lodge, which has market priced beer and $2 large soft serve cones, as well as various other sundry items which might be needed. Bring your own firewood though, because they are almost $9 a bundle.  Also enjoyed the nature trail - we had it all to ourselves when we went and the sights are not very different than what you would find at the much more crowded Hoh.

reviews.author: Shawn O.
reviews.text: Wonderful campgroud.  Our family was thrilled to be able to stay in site D024.

reviews.author: Lindsay F.
reviews.text: Great location, good facilities. Tucked into the trees, but a short walk from the beach. Interesting ranger programs available.

reviews.author: Elizabeth W.
reviews.text:
Site C1, it's quite small and close to neighbors, but good for a smaller tent. The location of the campground it very nice, close to the beach, but quite remote if you want any services. FYI if you want to do laundry in Forks, they close at 5pm. 
We walked from beach 4 to Ruby beach during closure and we were the only people we saw all day, it was amazing. Bald and Golden eagles fishing, otters and starfish. Be prepared for rain.

reviews.author: Kathy H.
reviews.text: Plan for rain or cool, cloudy weather. Bring extra toilet paper and hand soap, bathrooms run out of TP daily. No fresh water access for E/F loops as the outside faucet has been "under construction" for past 12 months. Why is this? Camping in D Loop can be dangerous due to cliff erosion. Fencing is gone in some places, road runs near to cliff and drop-offs are not marked with warning signs. Potentially very dangerous, why is there no warning signs or barricades to keep kids from falling off the cliff, especially at night when going to restrooms? Outside lights at amphitheater are rusted, broken off and don't work. Why are there still there? Amphitheater area looks especially trashy. Overall condition of Kalaloch has deteriorated compared to a couple years ago.

reviews.author: Sarah H.
reviews.text: Ruby Beach, Hoh Rain Forest, long walks on Kalaloch Beach.  Know your pad length - most sites are very short and cannot accommodate an RV and/or travel trailer, making unhitching mandatory then parking your vehicle sideways or somewhere else.

reviews.author: Rudolf M.
reviews.text: It's a must-see destination with an very clean campground

reviews.author: Elizabeth W.
reviews.text: So close to awesome beaches! Campsites are decently not on top of each other. Noise from the road but not terrible. Biggest complaint was no place to dump dishwater // water faucets were a real hike away from our site.

reviews.author: Shalena S.
reviews.text: The beach is magical and we enjoyed our time in the water and on the sand. The campsites are small and very close by so if you want privacy it’s not the place. There is ample space to feel expansive on the beach though. The host is amazing and overall a wonderful camping experience for us.

reviews.author: Alyssa J.
reviews.text: Not very private and right next to the highway, you can hear everything. Big plus you’re right next to the beach.

reviews.author: Kristin S.
reviews.text: The Beach Kalaloch is one of the best in the world. We walked for miles on the wide sand. In the morning we were treated to the sight of many orcas just off the shore going up and down in the waves. Just fabulous

reviews.author: Josephin K.
reviews.text: Love the location of this campground. It gets very crowded and the restrooms could need more cleaning sometimes.

reviews.author: Ariane H.
reviews.text: The cabins were the perfect combo of rustic and comfortable. Loved doing fires on the beach at night and the front desk and restaurant staff were excellent. Would have liked a few more seafood options on the menu, but the restaurant was a very nice amenity with a great view!

reviews.author: Brittany W.
reviews.text: Great campsite, I've stayed here once before and the bathrooms are always clean and the campsite feels safe and fun. It is great being so close to the ocean, as well as Lake Quinault and Rialto for day trips. The campsites are small but one of a kind, each on feels different. I've always stayed in the A loop furthest from the coast, and there's always logs and paths to explore.

reviews.author: Bhanu S.
reviews.text: My trailer had to jack-knife to fit into the camping spot and there were some good samaritans who helped me out, couldn't ask for anything more for a good start.  later on sunset, night walk and morning golf on the beach was just enough for my way of fun.  My kids played baseball and other things.

reviews.author: Katy C.
reviews.text: Quiet campground with respectful visitors

reviews.author: Melissa J.
reviews.text: Too many people parked in the road in campsite to move safely.

reviews.author: Anthony R.
reviews.text: Very good campsite, beaches were more crowded than normal but still easy to get to and plenty of things to do at each one..

reviews.author: Mary W.
reviews.text:
Great beach to walk on. Fun hiking trail loops out from camp with multiple waterfalls. Decent privacy between sites with all the trees and shrubs. 
Surprised there was no soap available in the bathrooms. C5 is not recommended for a Car Rooftop Tent. Short slanted parking but I had a way to level the car.

reviews.author: Sarah O.
reviews.text: Such a lovely spot - and even though we were in the 'undesirable' back row nearest the road, the campsite was spacious and comfortable and the noise level wasn't at all troubling during the night. The Lodge is handy for picking up snacks and drinks, and the beach is just magnificent! We'll go back for sure.

reviews.author: Molly  D.
reviews.text: Beautiful location, lots of big fat trees- it felt like a fairy garden for the kids.

reviews.author: Christopher l.
reviews.text:
This is a nice secluded campground with good privacy. It's towards the end of loop A. I was really worried about bugs and mosquito as this spot was heavily shaded and got hardly any sunlight. But I didn't have any issues even at night even after a downpour the day prior to my arrival. Plus it stayed fairly dry even with the downpour. It's the closest camp spot to Kalaloch Creek Nature trail and bear protected food storage. Bathrooms and water are close around the corner and two camp spots away.  Overall this was a great spot with lots of trees and shade.

My only complaint is that I wanted a spot where I could get the beach breeze, see a nice beach sunset, and with quick beach access. But if you don't mind walking a little it's a good spot to camp.

reviews.author: Scott L.
reviews.text: It was tough for me to find the information I was looking for, but everything ended up great. We stayed in site A28 which fit my 33 foot trailer and tow vehicle perfectly. I did have to back down the road the wrong way to fit into the spot, but it was not difficult, and the site was very spacious and right across the street from the ocean. Despite the rain (stayed June 1st thru the 4th) I would definitely stay here again! Bathrooms in the A loop were dated, but kept nice and clean. Access to the beach was amazing.

reviews.author: Ryan S.
reviews.text: Camp site and amenities were in excellent condition and the morning walks on the beach were unbeatable.

reviews.author: Margot F.
reviews.text: Of the 3 different campgrounds we stayed at in Olympic, this one was our favorite! Amazing location with some great spots overlooking the ocean if you can get them. I believe both of us had some phone service here. Con with all of these campsites is I found the bathrooms often didn't have soap or paper towels. Great proximity to Ruby Beach, Quinault Lake, and the Hoh rainforest.

reviews.author: Kerrie B.
reviews.text: beautiful campground! beach here is amazing

reviews.author: Tim H.
reviews.text:
Everything was in order and nicely taken care of.

We did have a concern with Recreation.gov. When we previewed availability for some of the more desired campsites in Kalalock 181 days prior to booking season, they showed blocked for the entire summer. We kept an eye on their “unlocking” during open reserving and they did not unlock. Website icons showed blocked, not booked.When we arrived 6 months later, they were occupied. (E9 for example).

reviews.author: Dale R.
reviews.text: Beautiful beach side sites nestled in tall pine trees.  Sites were spacious.  Restrooms were clean.  RV dump easy to access and use.  Would definitely like to return.

reviews.author: Danielle M.
reviews.text: Loved my campsite of D27. Great view of the beach. Beautiful campground. Very clean.

reviews.author: Kelsy K.
reviews.text: The stay at the campground was absolutely wonderful. I felt safe and enjoyed the beach so close to us <3 we traveled along the 101 but mostly kept to beach next to the campground. We plan to 100% come again :)

reviews.author: Robin S.
reviews.text: We walked north to Ruby Beach and had it to ourselves, sense the parking lot was closed for it.

reviews.author: Thomas C.
reviews.text: The experience REALLY depends on the site at this campground. The “road-side” sites are small, close together, and hard to get in and out of (not to mention road noise and campfire smoke). The “beach side” sites are mainly awesome-great views, easier access, less smoke. If I’d have had one of those sites I’d probably give the campground 4 instead of 2.

reviews.author: Allen A.
reviews.text: Great spaced camping sites. You are not "cheek to jowl" with your fellow campers.  Beach is fantastic.  Campground staff are not obtrusive.

reviews.author: Claire R.
reviews.text: Great Pacific Northwest beach experience.  Sunsets were gorgeous with cool nights and warm sunshine for 3 of our 4 days.  Rainy and cool our last day, but that just adds to the rainforest/beach feel.

reviews.author: Ryan H.
reviews.text: Really great as always. Tree of life is a great easy stroll to see.

reviews.author: Ann B.
reviews.text: Beautiful spacious campsites. Campground was well maintained and clean.

reviews.author: Brittany D.
reviews.text: We hada wonderful campsite and really enjoyed our time. Unfrotunetly we were by the road and were able to hears cars going by throughout the night. But overall it was a wonderful campsite and I would stay again.

reviews.author: Lance S.
reviews.text: Kalaloch is one of my most favorite spots to go camping.  The weather is always unpredictable but regardless, it's always a wonderful experience. The campground is well maintained and the bathrooms are nice, but lacking showers.  There's a small store a short walk down by the lodge if you forget something.  Walking on the beach, flying a kite or watching whales (we saw one) are relaxing activities.  Be sure and bring what you need, because there are very limited shopping opportunities within 20 or so miles.

reviews.author: Brianna C.
reviews.text: Great campground!

reviews.author: Calli J.
reviews.text: We loved it here! Will make it a go-to camping spot. We had one of the sites by the road which wasn't a big deal overnight and we were still surrounded by big old beautiful trees. Walking distance from the Lodge if you need firewood/supply/a cocktail from the bar. Would recommend booking early for an ocean view spot. Someone stole our wood which was a bummer but other than that positive experience!

reviews.author: Kara E.
reviews.text: Good tent site. Didn't experience roots like the site description stated.  Close to beach access.

reviews.author: Brooke C.
reviews.text: Great place with lovely camp sites.

reviews.author: VASILIY  S.
reviews.text: Some camping sites not suitable for RV and yet available for RV reservations. That only make camping trip not enjoyable and hassle free, but wearing and worrisome.

reviews.author: Kristen E.
reviews.text: Clean restrooms, good beach access, private campsites. We reserved c15 and c17 for a larger family and those two sites worked great together

reviews.author: Zoran L.
reviews.text: Even though the specs for this site state only a 5'x5' tent space (which tent is only 5' long??) I had no issues setting up my 7.5'x4.5' tent (2 person). A larger tent would fit but there wouldn't be much space left over. I guess 10'x7' should fit easily, maybe a bit more. There's no view from this site as there are thick bushes blocking the view. There's a view 70ft away.

reviews.author: Kelly H.
reviews.text: This is a nice campground on the coast a near lots of great beaches. You can hear the highway from many sites, so choose carefully

reviews.author: Marco L.
reviews.text: Loved the place and the location. I’ll definitely go back again

reviews.author: Rachel O.
reviews.text: After my first stay at Kalaloch, I knew I’d be back! This is a great spot to stay if exploring the many spots around the coast and Natl Park. There are multiple trails from the campground leading a short distance to the beach. My campsite was private and those nearby were friendly and abided by noise curfew. Peaceful and enjoyable place to make your home away from home.

reviews.author: Cindy C.
reviews.text: Beautiful location but the campsites are insanely small. Despite all the caveats about maximum size, we still had a neighbor across the way with at least a 30’ long trailer plus a pickup truck. No one polices the policy. The park should consider reconfiguring or removing sites and making them more reasonable. Also, both bathrooms were filthy and smelled. I would rather use my outdoor toilet!

reviews.author: William S.
reviews.text: Gorgeous location and campground

reviews.author: lori s.
reviews.text: I didn't like the camp host. Just sat at his trailer and scowled as. I walked past

reviews.author: shamus n.
reviews.text: Well kept campground with friendly host and park ranger.

reviews.author: Nicholas  R.
reviews.text: Absolutely terrible, nothing like sleeping 5 feet away from the constant roar of diesel trucks. This is not camping. Awful experience.

reviews.author: Rand C.
reviews.text: Site F002 was good location but short and skinny. We found it very private.  The map indicates it is on the shoreline but there is no view due to vegetation.  The walkway access to the beach is near the overflow lot. Easy walk down to beach where we saw lots of interesting things.   I parked the truck sideways in front of trailer to fit in.  Got a note on my windshield from our host that I had to move to the overflow lot.  Walking around the campground I saw at least 10 other tow vehicles which had also parked in front of their trailers as I did.  I was the only one with a note I could see and the only one who moved to the overflow lot.  GRRRR but ok.  This campground is shady.  Not enough sun to keep batteries charged with solar. The bathrooms were clean and had running water.  Also used the dump station once, which was easy access. You will need to exit by driving through loop D of campground to turnaround.  There was also a fresh water fill past the dump station at a safe distance from the dump.  It was great to see the fresh water was not right next to the dump station. In all we had an enjoyable visit and I would return here. Ruby Beach was the highlight of our adventures here.  We went twice at low tide and once at high tide.  Lots of ocean life like starfish to see here.  I understand the access to Ruby is closing July 2022.  Try to schedule your visit to avoid this closure.  We also went to the Hoh Rainforest one day.  Make sure to take your rain gear up there.  Stop at the little store/cafe on the way up.  It is an interesting  visit.  They serve a great breakfast.  We enjoyed the morning hikes at Hoh.  The afternoon got very crowded.

reviews.author: Alexandria F.
reviews.text: Such a beautiful spot - try to get a campsite with a view of the ocean! Also definitely check out the Tree of Life. I loved it here even with the rain!

reviews.author: Katherine S.
reviews.text: Fantastic location right above the beach. The campground was planned well with some privacy between sites, but most sites were easily accessible by car or RV. Campfire rings with an adjustable grill made for easy cooking. Local firewood can be purchased less than a mile down the road at the lodge store. The Tree of Life is just a short walk down the beach.

reviews.author: Janet P.
reviews.text: Had a great time.

reviews.author: KERI H.
reviews.text: A beautiful place to be rain or shine

reviews.author: Steve W.
reviews.text: Very clean, Great location. Our family love this place!

reviews.author: Lara V.
reviews.text:
The maintenance guys were frankly unfriendly and unwelcoming despite our attempts at conversation. They were borderline hostile and gave off a weird vibe.
The camp hosts had 'off duty' on their campers every time we went by, including during prime check in times. We were okay, but it created chaos for other campers.

reviews.author: Richard S.
reviews.text: We have camped here many times.  The campground is pleasant and right next to the ocean.  The nearby beaches, including Ruby Beach, are amazing!  We plan to come back as often as possible.  We do notice that the facilities, beach access stairs, and sites are showing their age and could use some maintenance.

reviews.author: Robert H.
reviews.text: Great campground!

reviews.author: Daniel P.
reviews.text: I was camping in a tent, it was not very warm and the second day it rained so I left a day early. Have to get me a travel trailer then it would not be as bad.

reviews.author: Herbert H.
reviews.text: Booking a site and the advise to find the site was very easy. An excellent place to walk on the beach.

reviews.author: Cheryl F.
reviews.text: Loved the campground at Kalaloch…great spots, roomy, and near the beach! Had lots of fun here…great time!

reviews.author: Kenny M.
reviews.text: shhh, don't tell anyone about this wonderful place

reviews.author: Matt R.
reviews.text: Great site, bathhouse was clean. Beach was amazing.

reviews.author: Georgina V.
reviews.text: Beautiful campground with beach access and clean bathrooms. Can’t go wrong!

reviews.author: laura j.
reviews.text: Very peaceful and clean place to camp, def will recommend to others 👌

reviews.author: Garry M.
reviews.text: Beautiful campsite with good privacy between sites and convenient beach access. Most sites are small but will accommodate smaller RVs. Restrooms were clean. Having to pay to use the dump station even though we were camping there was a surprise and disappointment.

reviews.author: Camie A.
reviews.text: This place is amazing - right on the coast. I was a bit unprepared for the tiny campsites and the complete lack of privacy though. I should have figured it out my the measurements but it didn't really register at the time. If you are a camping in a vehicle you will want to have complete window coverings. Also would have been helpful to have info about firewood (or lack of it!) in advance. Have to go to the lodge to get it, and when I went they were out. It was too late to start driving around to find some elsewhere. Even with that I'd go back. It's a beautiful place.

reviews.author: Janet C.
reviews.text: Great place to camp with dogs.  Lots of beach areas to explore as well as the FS trails near Lake Quinault and elsewhere.  Perfect weather in early June.

reviews.author: Jana C.
reviews.text: Although it rained all weekend, our site by the water was perfect!  Just the sound was enough to make for a successful camping weekend.

reviews.author: Caryn A.
reviews.text: Kalaloch is one of our favorite campgrounds. All of those incredible beaches to walk on and the rainforest to explore. We'll definitely be back.

reviews.author: David H.
reviews.text: Always a beautiful campground and well-maintained

reviews.author: Megan N.
reviews.text: One of our favorite spots! An annual tradition.

reviews.author: Jessica M.
reviews.text: nice coastal campsite with clean grounds, access to water and restrooms (heated!)

reviews.author: Camille A.
reviews.text: What a beautiful campground! We had one of the ocean view sites and I can truly say it was one of the most beautiful campgrounds we have ever stayed at! The rain even held off on us for the night and we got to experience a lovely sunset! 10/10 would book again!

reviews.author: Elizabeth S.
reviews.text: Literally on the beach!! We were amazed at space and quietness of the grounds. The bathrooms were not the greatest, the hand dryers didn’t work...but they were clean. Ib100% recommend this camp ground!

reviews.author: becca p.
reviews.text: A beautiful setting not very well managed- bathrooms dirty, garbage overflowing, too many people and cars at the sites, no real ranger presence especially after hours. Sad to see this so mismanaged.

reviews.author: Allison S.
reviews.text: We had a horrible campsite D9 the first night but the ranger helped us out the next day and gave us an excellent water view spot that had been released :)

reviews.author: Fima M.
reviews.text:
Tremendous view from the coastal campsites! We will definitely be returning here. Easy reservation process.
Only downside (or upside?) was near zero reception with verizon wireless.

reviews.author: Jennifer P.
reviews.text: Beautiful campground and easy access to the beach!

reviews.author: Charles K.
reviews.text: Nice quiet park, easy access to the beach.

reviews.author: Chance  R.
reviews.text: Incredible campground with amazing sounds of the ocean. Our site was a 30 second walk to beach access.

reviews.author: Kristin E.
reviews.text: Campground is in a forest between the beach and highway. Some highway sounds heard from my campsite located near the highway. Easy access to the Kalaloch Beaches and the Kalaloch Creek Nature Trail.

reviews.author: Anne D.
reviews.text: We enjoyed our trip to Olympic National Park and to Kalaloch campground. The services are excellent and it's so lovely to camp by the ocean!

reviews.author: Zowie A.
reviews.text: This is an incredibly busy campground in the summer with people loudly enjoying outdoor movies outside their giant RVs, projecting LED lights into the surrounding trees (obscuring the stars and setting moon), and drunkenly playing "Never Have I Ever" at top volume. Basic campground etiquette appeared to be a foreign concept to the vast majority of campers, and the number of campfires merrily dancing during a total burn ban smacked of the self-centered entitlement of FOMO fueled, social-media-obsessed 'campers' that seem to have taken over natural spaces over the past years. Why so many people drive many hours to the edge of a wilderness coast full of beauty and natural history to blast Ariana Grande and never look up from their red solo cups is astounding.

reviews.author: Tina A.
reviews.text: This campground is absolutely amazing and our family keeps coming back to it time and time again!

reviews.author: Alexa V.
reviews.text: Amazing camp and beach. Our campsite was big, however, the parking spot for the van is on a noticeable incline so plan to bring leveling gear or lie on an incline. That being said, we slept just fine and had amazing walks on Kalaloch which was so close to our camp site. Highly recommended to anyone and everyone.

reviews.author: Harry T.
reviews.text: Very nice well maintained campground.

reviews.author: Fred A.
reviews.text: We had a wonderful stay at southbeach.  We had reservations at Kalaloch but had a great water site at South Beach and decided not to move.  The camp host at South Beach are the best.  They are golden in everything they do.  So many friendly people there. I'm sad to hear South beach may go to reservations.  We drove thru the main park and saw so many no shows and prime sites sat open for days. You need to fix your reservation cancels.  I received a conformation 1 week ahead of our reservations, you need a confirmation reply button so people and say yay or ney if they are coming.  It was hard to see people turn away when spots were left open. Kalaloch is the best have been coming for years. Be back soon.

reviews.author: Diane B.
reviews.text: Appreciated being able to get a site.  I am grateful for the reservation period and I am also grateful for the times when there are no reservations.  I do wish the lodges restaurant would have been open but am grateful for the little store by the lodges.  Thanks for being there and such a lovely place to camp and use as a home base for hiking and going out into the Hoh rain forest.

reviews.author: Mary K.
reviews.text:
Kalaloch Campground was beautiful!  Bathrooms were clean as was the campground in general.  Just a couple of suggestions.  The campsite was good but it was obvious that previous campers had driven off the pavement as there were tire tracks in the wet ground.  It would have been nice it if the space were raked or something to remove those before we arrived.  Also, the table was at quite a slant and the space seemed to have better possible locations for it.  

Appreciate all the park hosts do for a great camping experience!  Thank you.

reviews.author: Sandi R.
reviews.text: A beautiful place to camp!!

reviews.author: Sandy  U.
reviews.text: Love this place right on the ocean. Great walking beach  clean restrooms and camp ground

reviews.author: Elise I.
reviews.text: I find it ironic that they enforce a mask mandate in the restrooms but can't be bothered to provide any soap for hand washing. Also they leave the windows in the restroom cracked which leads to every mosquito in the vicinity to gather inside it. You can't use the restroom without literally getting swarmed by mosquitoes.

reviews.author: Brendan W.
reviews.text: Great campground, quiet, awesome views, clean facilities

reviews.author: Michael C.
reviews.text: Great location on the ocean

reviews.author: Mia M.
reviews.text: Great location, but small and very narrow sites for campers and trailers.

reviews.author: Michelle M.
reviews.text: Campsites next to the ocean are amazing!

reviews.author: Steven H.
reviews.text: Fabulous scenery

reviews.author: Shaun P.
reviews.text: I absolutely love this campground!  Big mature trees, moss, ferns -- feels very Jurassic.  It is in a RAIN FOREST, so be prepared for cool, chilly, damp conditions.  Also, BELIEVE the vehicle restrictions!  We heard tales of woe from several families who got stuck, broke an axle, etc., trying to wedge into spaces that were too small.  There truly is no extra room.

reviews.author: Brenda S.
reviews.text: Amazing Beach and campground especially if you get an ocean view!

reviews.author: Michael T.
reviews.text: There are plenty of spacious campsites at Kalaloch.   The restrooms are well heated.  Camping in the rain forest right next to the beach is a treat.  Plenty of trees to hang a tarp on for the rainy weather.  The trees also protect from the strong winds that sometimes come ashore.  A million logs on the beach create a haven for children to laugh, play, and build a fort.  The nearby freshwater river is a great place to get a refreshing swim.

reviews.author: Kerri H.
reviews.text: What a great place to be one with nature

reviews.author: April K.
reviews.text: Kalaloch is my favorite park! The campground is always clean, the bathrooms are clean. The views are breathtaking.  Watching a meteor shower with the Milky Way showing is an experience we'll never forget. We had a rainy day, and took the opportunity to drive into Forks and visit the museum and the Twilight tourist stuff. The kids are already planning our trip next year!!

reviews.author: Kirsti R.
reviews.text: The only problem is it is too crowded.  So don't come and leave it all for us!

reviews.author: Matt A.
reviews.text: The MOST beautiful camping ground I’ve ever been to

reviews.author: Malia M.
reviews.text: The campsites are very small and right on top of each other, so there's very little privacy or the feeling of "wilderness." That being said, the sites are very well maintained, the concrete picnic tables are excellent (though sometimes in strange places that make setting up a tent difficult), and the views from the front sites on the coast are stunning. A warning, the sites that run along the 101 highway are very much open to the road and can be seen by everyone. Plus the road noise is significant, definitely try not to book those, unless it's in the A loop.

reviews.author: Amber S.
reviews.text: Favorite campground

reviews.author: Jim L.
reviews.text: The park does not communicate clearly the definition of vehicle. A licensed trailer is considered a vehicle. Signs saying two vehicles per site, include the trailer you pulled.

reviews.author: Lindsay O.
reviews.text: Gorgeous Campground, very clean bathrooms, easy trails to the beach, fun for the whole fam!

reviews.author: Lisa O.
reviews.text: Beautiful camping area next to the beach, awesome views a short walk away, lots of shade amidst large trees. The facilities  were clean and the whole experience very peaceful. A well attended nature talk in the evening about sea creatures explained a lot about animals and aspects of climate change.

reviews.author: Tamera M.
reviews.text: Great time. Sites were well spaced out and big. Short walk to the ocean. Bathrooms were clean and well-maintained.

reviews.author: Brenda S.
reviews.text: Amazing campsite with ocean view!

reviews.author: Jeff P.
reviews.text: Wow…So breath-taking! The ranger and Camp Host were extremely friendly and helpful.

reviews.author: Etana K.
reviews.text: Amazing 4-mile wide flat beach with easy access, so lovely.  Many amazing sites with ocean views.  A great place, we'll definitely be back.

reviews.author: Angelique B.
reviews.text: Nice campground and facilities clean. Staff friendly and helpful!! Make sure you watch the sunset!!

reviews.author: Bethel F.
reviews.text: We’ve been there twice. Our first camping experience and it was amazing. We will definitely coming back again next year. The location is the best and I felt safe for my family. Highly recommended camping site, especially for first timers.

reviews.author: Lorinda R.
reviews.text: We enjoyed our stay very much. all the campgrounds and facilities were clean and I felt safe for me and my family. Thank you.

reviews.author: Chrissy and Micah L.
reviews.text: This campground lives up to the expectations that it is in truly one of the most beautiful places on Earth.

reviews.author: Kevork S.
reviews.text: Beautiful and quiet campground. The nature trail is easy and beautiful. Ruby beach near by is beautiful at sunset.

reviews.author: Anthony R.
reviews.text: Campground was very nice, it was mostly quiet at night also.. beaches in the area are great..

reviews.author: Mark M.
reviews.text: Got lucky and scored an oceanfront site for a night. Great location all the way around.

reviews.author: Frank P.
reviews.text:
The campground itself is very basic, and wedged between busy US Hwy 101 and cliffs that provide minimal views of the ocean due to shrub and tree growth.  Although you can't see the ocean from most of the CG unless you have one of the very few view sites, you can hear the ocean when not drowned out by logging trucks and other traffic on 101.  There are a few paths down to the ocean and beach which, in this stretch, is fairly unremarkable but easily walked at lower tides.  The campground does provide a launch pad for driving to other beaches which are more interesting and fun.
Very limited fresh water sources in the CG.  Dump station requires RV's driving through much of the CG (both going and coming on single road) to the "pleasure" of campers on that road.  Limited restrooms.

reviews.author: Paul T.
reviews.text: Total experience was great. Site host and rangers were great.

reviews.author: Walter F.
reviews.text:
Camp host were the best
Fishing for surf perch and seeing the grey whales EVERYDAY was with thousands more than you charged me

reviews.author: Jeremy S.
reviews.text:
We stayed at the Kalaloch Campground, site C005. This site is in the forest, so it has plenty of shade and wasn’t too windy. There was a bit of highway noise, though. There’s no view of the coast from the site, but it isn’t a long walk to the beach. This site was close to the bathroom, but it wasn’t too noisy.

I strongly recommend trying to get to beach 4 (3 miles north of here) at low tide. It’s a bit of a scramble to get to the bottom, but this is a good rocky beach for tide pool viewing.

reviews.author: Kaila R.
reviews.text: This was our 28th summer of camping at Kalaloch. A family tradition we cherish. Aways something new to explore and favorite spots to visit. We love it!

reviews.author: Nancy H.
reviews.text: No soap in bathroom

reviews.author: Sara E.
reviews.text: Such a clean campground!! The hosts and rangers are top notch. I can’t wait to go back

reviews.author: Nancy H.
reviews.text: no bad campsites, some closer to the beach view than others but the beach is a short walk away. Beautiful location.

reviews.author: Shannon W.
reviews.text: This area is spectacularly beautiful, with the beach and the forest. But the site we reserved was pretty bad. It was the last one available so we didn’t have a choice. Site 069; it was right by the bathrooms and garbage dumpsters, so the smell was pretty bad. And highway noise, including loud logging trucks, kept us up at night. The sites along the bluff are amazing and you’d be lucky to snag one! I’d go back if I can manage to reserve a site away from the highway. Very busy when we went in August, and every spot was taken. I wouldn’t chance going without a reservation!

reviews.author: Chelsey T.
reviews.text: Incredible views, pristine campgrounds with spacious sites, amazing beach access and exceptionally helpful, friendly staff and volunteers!

reviews.author: Kiran J.
reviews.text: Campground right next to the beach. We had a good time and is a great option to explore Olympic National Park.

reviews.author: Harlie S.
reviews.text: Great place to stay. Very clean restrooms. Not far from the Hoh rainforest or Forks.

reviews.author: Jared M.
reviews.text: Amazing location and beach, but the ground is pretty rocky and it got very cold at night for summer

reviews.author: Keith B.
reviews.text:
We've been coming here, twice a year, for >40 years from Seattle.  It really couldn't be a more beautify place, especially when the sun comes out.  The Washington Coast is truly rugged and amazing here from Ruby to South Beach.  The restrooms on the north loops were recently remodeled and are nice.  However, I'm not sure how much longer Kalaloch will be around.  The cliff side erosion has really increased this last couple years.  Several sites have been lost and several more are on the verge of collapse.  The lodge lost the beach access and the gazebo last winter (stairs rebuilt for the summer season).  A couple cabins maybe lost in the next few years if nothing is done to protect the hillside.

Don't come here for the cellular/internet access.  You'll find it missing (and be glad for it)!

reviews.author: Priscilla T.
reviews.text: super fun trip. very clean and no bugs. everyone was quiet and respectful around us with no music blasting. beach was beautiful as well.

reviews.author: wilmer d.
reviews.text: Nice ocean viw

reviews.author: Marit Z.
reviews.text: My first time camping in a campground.  Had a lovely time.  I even asked the ranger if there was a better spot open as my reserved spot was totally shaded and she happily found me a new spot.  Great people there.

reviews.author: Nicole D.
reviews.text: Clean campground just steps away from the beach. They spots were very roomy (I had a tent). I was in a spot that butts up along the 101 and the woosh from the cars/trucks was very loud but seemed pretty non existent over night so it didn't bother me at all.

reviews.author: Pam  B.
reviews.text: Too many dogs. Dog barking woke me up every morning and dogs were not on leases on the beach. Over four days trying to watch birds, the dogs were always interfering. I went to Ruby beach low tide only to be greeted by a unleashed Doberman pincher at the top of the trail, it scared and angered me. Not what I want to experience after this early morning outing!

reviews.author: Jenise R.
reviews.text: Great beach, clean restrooms, sites are a little tight but understandable. Nice common picnic table in Loop A for sunset.

reviews.author: Sophia O.
reviews.text: I love this campground! The close access to the beach is wonderful. Even though there is a burn ban in effect and we could not make a campfire, the experience was still great. The campground host was very helpful! When we arrived there was someone at our campsite and the campground host handled it quickly and kindly. We tent camped and it was chilly at night even in the middle of August. It was misty too, so its good to bring rain gear. Overall a beautiful place, I will definitely be back!

reviews.author: Austin F.
reviews.text: Beautiful place to camp. Be sure to check out the 'Tree of Life' on the beach when you visit.

reviews.author: Dave H.
reviews.text: Wonderful beach, great places to hike and watching the whales.

reviews.author: Jan A.
reviews.text: Great beach!!  The restrooms don't have showers or hot water, but otherwise the camping is enjoyable.  The sites along the beach are amazing.  Most of the others are large but quite shady.  It was cool when we went and since fires weren't allowed the campsites were chilly.  This wasn't a huge problem since we just had to walk down to the beach to see the sun.

reviews.author: Renee G.
reviews.text: We love Kalaloch (and the Quinault lodge) and try to make it out there at least once a year.  This year though I was surprised by how seemingly understaffed and understocked everything was (like the stores, etc.).  Still a wonderful time thank you

reviews.author: Jonathon K.
reviews.text: We had a full beach view, which was beautiful. There was limited shade at our site, but enough to get by. Many of the sites have excellent shade, but don't expect any given site to have good shade: If you plan to park a vehicle midday in the summer, make sure there is nothing heat sensitive or it may cook, even if the outdoor air temperature is in the 70's. The other campers were a little loud, opening and closing car doors well past 10 pm, but other than that, the ocean provides almost perfect white noise. We plan on returning to Olympic national park largely because of this campground!

reviews.author: Kari B.
reviews.text: We had a fantastic time camping! Beautiful campground and beaches. The only thing that could make it better was to have showers!

reviews.author: Helen I.
reviews.text:
Beautiful location. The ocean is all you need. Large campsite at C009 with shade and privacy but not isolated. Restrooms were basic, but clean and flushing toilets. Soap would have been lovely. 
Great campground. Will be back!

reviews.author: Claire S.
reviews.text: The A-loop is right off of the main road and the tent sites are small and offer very little privacy from neighbors (we were in A64). Our first night was pretty awful, but we managed to switch to the F-loop for our second night and had a lovely campsite where the sound of the ocean drowned out the road noise.

reviews.author: Sofia B.
reviews.text: We had a wonderful time at this campground! The facilities were spotless, the camping sites were great. We stayed at two different ones during our time there, one by the water in section E and one in the woodsy area in section B. Both were great and very different experiences. We saw sea otters, whales, and lots of birds while there!

reviews.author: Susan T.
reviews.text: Campsite was completely full and the beach was the most crowded I’ve seen.

reviews.author: Zachary K.
reviews.text: Considering, it is a very heavily used, hard to get into campground, it would be nice to add modern restrooms including showers.

reviews.author: Dorothy G.
reviews.text: We love it at Kalaloch. It is a beautiful campground and walking on the beach is the best.

reviews.author: Lynda J.
reviews.text: One of the best views from the campground. We felt very fortunate to grab this spot! It is very exposed and gets no shade, so if you're in a tent make sure you have somewhere else to be around 1PM-4PM. It also gets a little chillier and windier at night, but other than that it is PERFECT!

reviews.author: Lynda J.
reviews.text: Campsite is right next to the road, where large trucks pass at high speeds. It would shake our entire tent and kept us up all night,

reviews.author: Colby A.
reviews.text: REALLY GROSS BATHROOMS and no management presence.

reviews.author: Brian w.
reviews.text: Wonderful!

reviews.author: Lisa B.
reviews.text: Roomy campsite near the ocean on loop D. We camped in a campervan so it was nice to have access to the flush toilets and bathroom sink. Nice camp store where we bought white wine and takeout restaurant. The beach is just a few stairways down to the shore,  Would definitely camp here again!

reviews.author: Kyle S.
reviews.text: We love the campground. Just wish there were showers

reviews.author: Natalia  A.
reviews.text: So close to the ocean, your nook has so much overgrowth so there's still privacy from other campers, and the smells and sounds are wondrous.

reviews.author: Sarah M.
reviews.text:
Sadly it’s just not the same experience as the 30+ years we have had before. The rangers are so young and prideful. There’s is no consistency in the things they demanded of campers (heaven forbid you rest your bikes on a bush or bring up a rock from the beach). And the hosts aren’t much better. The store was almost empty most days we went in and both the lodge and store were ill stocked when ordering food items.
We do still love the camp ground though and it was extra beautiful with not having fires. The stars were gorgeous! Also updated bathrooms were awesome!

reviews.author: Michael S.
reviews.text: Beach setting.  Even though we were closer to the road, it wasn't super loud from road traffic and felt private.  The bathrooms felt new and were very clean with water close by.

reviews.author: Seth C.
reviews.text: We stayed in A33 and wasn’t certain what to expect.  The site is large and private, facing towards the ocean and a short walk to the beach access path and the bathrooms.  The campsite sits right on the beach but with some tree protection ruin.  The beach itself is huge and sandy.  Best of all is the short hike to the restaurant at Kalaloch lodge which served great takeout food which we ate in the outdoor patio overlooking the ocean.  A 10 out of 10 camping experience.

reviews.author: Brad W.
reviews.text:
Kalaloch is a beautiful campground. amazing Beach.
Staff was friendly campground was clean and welcoming
This was 10 years of time with our Grandchildren

reviews.author: Shalena S.
reviews.text: We enjoyed our stay at Kalaloch campground which is right off the beach. Beach can be windy and cold even in summer but the campground is tucked in and protected except for the sites adjacent to the beach. Sites are quite close to each other and that’s what you can expect from a popular campground. Nice place to go with a group of families. Kids can bike around and play on the beach. Host was amazing!

reviews.author: Justin C.
reviews.text: Had a good time. Campground was clean and mostly quiet at night.  I wish campgrounds would look into banning amplified music in campsites.  The noise pollution takes away from the camping experience and carries well past the boundaries of the campsite it belongs to.

reviews.author: Amy B.
reviews.text: This was a beautiful campground with easy access to the beach. Bring leveling blocks and hats/mittens. It was cold at night (40s) and cool during the day (60s).

reviews.author: David L.
reviews.text: Great campground!  Campsites are pretty well spaced out.  Can walk to the beach in less than 5 minutes.  Can get pretty cold at night (as most of the WA coast is).  Walking distance to the Lodge which has a restaurant and a general store.

reviews.author: Karin H.
reviews.text: The campground was located right on the pacific coast. We walked right from our site onto the beach. We watched several beautiful sunsets over the water. The bathrooms were basically brand new. However there were no showers which would have been a nice addition.

reviews.author: Robert B.
reviews.text: We loved Kalaloch! The location was wonderful, the sites and restrooms were clean and fellow campers were courteous and friendly. A great way to end our Olympic adventure!

reviews.author: Tim B.
reviews.text: Beautiful camp site in the trees along with easy beach access.  The stars were also incredible at night from the beach.

reviews.author: Sandeep K.
reviews.text: Very beautiful spot and every trip we seem to find more areas to explore nearby!

reviews.author: Traysiah S.
reviews.text: We love it there! The bathrooms were new and clean. The camp site was private and surrounded by trees. The beach is one of the most spectacular beaches anywhere. And I lived in California for years. We woll be going there on a regular basis. Loved it!!!

reviews.author: Karen D.
reviews.text: Very noisy site on main road into campground. Road noise from 101 detracts from experience for the campsites close to road. Great hosts and rangers. Great beaches nearby.

reviews.author: Karen D.
reviews.text: Campsites that are close to road are extremely noisy due to passing traffic. No soap in bathrooms. Camp hosts and rangers were very friendly and helpful. Highly recommend searching for site away from 101.

reviews.author: Kiersten W.
reviews.text:
We were in A05 which was a roomy campsite, many were very small and closely situated. First time staying, we got in on a weekday. It was fine, a place to put a tent that is near the ocean. There were two dog piles in our campsite which was gross. Unfortunately we have seen more of this kind of careless regard for others of late. 

I can't say I highly reccomend Kalaloch campground but if you want to be near the beach, this will do. Bathroom by our site was dirty. There was not any hand soap offered so we had to bring our own hand soap when using the restroom which was a pain and pretty gross as I did not see anyone else come with soap. Provide the dang soap, don't be cheap.

No Verizon service.

reviews.author: Anne T.
reviews.text: This is a nice campground that's kept clean. Fair warning about the crows here though - if you turn your back on any food items/trash bags for more than 10 seconds they will go after it! Keep your food guarded at all times!

reviews.author: Priyanka S.
reviews.text: Loved this campground! Right by the beach. It was definitely loud past quiet hours when we were there- would have appreciated more rounds done by hosts/rangers. Campsites are fairly close to each other too. But overall the experience was awesome!

reviews.author: Will C.
reviews.text:
No water source on our side of campground.

Having at least cold water shower would be a major improvement.  Camping may include sleeping in tents but it shouldn't mean no showers for a week.

reviews.author: Dong Z.
reviews.text: Excellent campsite. It’s right on the beach

reviews.author: Shad H.
reviews.text: Wonderful campground and beautiful beaches

reviews.author: Lalena J.
reviews.text: If you go to the beach during low tide, there are some small tidepools filled with sea anemones and small eels and fish just to the left of the camping entrance. There are better and worse spots in the campground, so if you book early enough make sure to check out the pictures to make sure it fits your needs. We'll definitely be coming back and staying longer in the future. Bathroom and water were easily accessible. Beautiful campgrounds. Can't beat the beach.

reviews.author: Anton M.
reviews.text: Clean site, awesome views, ocean.

reviews.author: FRANCINE W.
reviews.text: Kalaloch has become a family tradition starting with my children and now being carried on with my grandchildren. The campsites are great, the beach is amazing - very low key and relaxing!

reviews.author: Allen G.
reviews.text: Access to the coast, Hoh Rain Forest, Beach 4 tidepools and the sea stacks make Kalaloch a great place to camp in the Olympic National Park.  Also, the rest rooms were clean and well maintained.  Our site facing the Pacific Coast made for unforgettable sunsets and terrific star gazing.

reviews.author: Walter F.
reviews.text:
The fishing was great, camp host Gene and Normal were above and beyond
The rangers were informative 
But the best thing about it was the Whales in the surf
One of those truly life’s events....

reviews.author: Daniel B.
reviews.text: Hard to reserve, but worth the effort.  Lots of tree cover, so solar was not working the entire time.  Cool temperature on the coast when inland was 100.  A bit too close to the 101 for my taste, traffic noise is very noticeable at 0600.  Obviously the sights overlooking the cliff are the best, and the most difficult to reserve.  Smaller is better here, large RV and rigs just won't fit in many spots.  Very disappointed in the lodge next door.  Walking there requires you to walk on the 101 hyway shoulder.  With children 1-10 this is a heart pounding effort trying to keep them clear of speeding traffic and large trucks driving south.  A protected pedestrian section would be helpful.

reviews.author: Shilo C.
reviews.text: Crowded campground, but quiet and pleasant. So close to the beach, ideal location.

reviews.author: Molly M.
reviews.text: We loved Kalaloch and were happy to get a camping site. Beach 4 was terrific!

reviews.author: Karthigeyan G.
reviews.text: Camping near a ocean is not match. The sound of waves and mood light is therapeutic. Felt more closer to nature. Must try place. Nights are getting colder even on a hot day, be prepared. Try to book a site that has sea very you will love it.

reviews.author: Christy D.
reviews.text: Unless you get the very best of sites, I’d recommend skipping this campground. The sites next to the road are incredibly noisy, with trucks traveling on 101 at near highway speeds. The ones next to the ocean are quiet, but not the one we had in the back. Otherwise site was beautiful, bathrooms were clean, and accessibility to the beach was great.

reviews.author: Christine L.
reviews.text: We had campsite #4 which was right by the road and very noisy most of the time. Also, there was a lot of traffic coming into the campgrounds as we were near the entrance. The campsite was spacious and fairly private otherwise. The beach itself is very sandy which many people love but we preferred Ruby Beach and spent much of our time on the other beaches in the area. There was only one urinal in the men's bathroom so there was usually a line which is unusual for a men's bathroom. We might come back and try other campsites further from the road if we can get one.

reviews.author: Jason C.
reviews.text:
A Beautiful campsite and so conveniently close to Kalaloch Beach.

Pro's: 
- Beautiful woods
- Proximity to beach

Cons:
- Hwy 101 noise
- Bathrooms didn't have soap or hooks for toiletry kits
- No showers (but knew that in advance)

reviews.author: Bryan G.
reviews.text: Well-maintained campground that was surprisingly not as busy considering how popular the Kaloloch beach area can be (granted this was a trip during the week). Easy to find and navigate campground, host is right at the entrance (easy to find), plenty of facilities and trash dumpsters. Wild animals are not an issue, but I wouldn't just leave things lying around either. Easy beach access (3-minute walk from any campsite tops). One downside for some people is that many campsites are across the road from another, so there is not much privacy. You often have to parallel park at most sites though, so you can use this as a bit of a wall. Does get chilly once the sun goes down, even in the summer. Bugs not too bad.

reviews.author: Amber S.
reviews.text: Beautiful campground, very helpful rangers and park hosts.

reviews.author: Birgitte M.
reviews.text: When we booked this site, the picture showed a site that had beach view.  Our site was buried in bush area.  Tent pad leveled down on both sides, so no matter how we turned the tent, our heads lay lower then our body.  This is a terrible tent site.

reviews.author: Lance S.
reviews.text: Always a great experience primarily because of the location.  The campground is old and many of the sites are very small, so be careful that your RV will fit.  They charge for use of the dump station on top of the camping fee.  There are no showers anywhere in the campground.  There are also no recycling facilities which I think ought to be a requirement inside a National Park.

reviews.author: Janna H.
reviews.text: Great campground it watch the ones that say road noise.  We knew it when we reserved as we didn’t have a choice due to availability.  The road noise is extreme although it does quiet down at night, but during the day, morning and evening the road noise is quite obnoxious.  With that said, loved the location, the nature walk, the beach and everything else.

reviews.author: Parke S.
reviews.text: This campsite was excellent, with a beautiful view, clean and semi-secluded site. Access to the beach was really close. The bathrooms were clean and the whole campground was amazing- I could not find a “bad” site!

reviews.author: Stephanie H.
reviews.text: Site D007 is close to the road but this didn‘t bother us too much. Lot‘s of shade - the sun didn‘t make it through on a cloudy day. Restrooms in loop D could have been cleaner - I  had the impression they were frequently used by day visitors.

reviews.author: Celeste B.
reviews.text: Such a special campground. Everyone was so quiet while we were there - I usually only heard the waves crashing on the beach.

reviews.author: Jennifer  P.
reviews.text: This is hands down one of the best campgrounds I’ve ever stayed at! We loved it so much, we came back a week later and took our chances on a waitlist! Site 11 was perfection- spacious, water views, a little path to enjoy beach view, etc. Can’t wait to come back some day!

reviews.author: Mark G.
reviews.text: Sites are VERY small and close together, though there is brush to give a sense of privacy, particularly on the outer side of the loops (inside the loops there is less privacy). We made the mistake of not reading our site description well: our site did not have back-in parking (parallel) which was inconvenient because we were using a truckbed tent… felt like we were sleeping in the road…but that was our fault not the campground’s fault.

reviews.author: Marcos M.
reviews.text: My campsite was easy to find. I went to the registration hut and two volunteers greeted me and let me know I could go ahead and set up my camp and no further registration was needed. The bathrooms were clean enough and well maintained although it did run out of soap :( but i brought my own so problem solved! Beautiful location, quiet neighbors, great experience.

reviews.author: JOHN AND JUNE B.
reviews.text: We had a great one night stay. Also has great day use area to watch ocean and whales.

reviews.author: Brandon W.
reviews.text: Bathrooms are crowded, small, outdated, disgusting. They were cleaned while we were there, but that doesn't change the fact that the same graffiti is etched into the stalls that was there 15 plus years ago. They are a major step down from other campgrounds such as Bogachiel state park, maybe because this is a national park and funding is limited. Also, beware of mice, raccoons, and crows. We had daily issues with all of these scavengers for the entire week we were there.

reviews.author: Brenda S.
reviews.text: Beautiful beach and campground. Wi-fi was not good but it was good to be unconnected!

reviews.author: Erika J.
reviews.text: We had the most beautiful campsite we have ever had.  Facilities were clean.  Water and dump station were available in the campground.  My only complaint is that we paid for two vehicles at the site but the ranger made us move one to the parking lot because it was touching the grass.

reviews.author: Andrea W.
reviews.text: Loved it here, will be making reservations next year!

reviews.author: Rachel E.
reviews.text: As always, Kaloach is a magical place and we love to visit here. However, the Campground host, Gene makes the magic disappear. As we were told by the rangers, we are not the first ones to have issues with him and he seems to get many complaints. Without going into detail we felt like we were somewhat targeted by him and had to get the rangers involved for him to back off and leave us alone. The other campground host was great and we highly recommend talking to him or the rangers instead of Gene.

reviews.author: Sarah B.
reviews.text: We stayed near the road, D7 but you could still hear the beach which was nice. Site was really big, could easily fit two small tents. Having the beach in walking distance was awesome.

reviews.author: PHILLIP L M.
reviews.text: Lovely area but campground needs updating badly.  Multiple sites on Hwy 101 which means logging trucks at all hours, dump station so close to sites the line blocks them, etc.

reviews.text: Kalaloch campground along the coast of Olympic National Park was very enjoyable.  Beach walks at Ruby Beach and Beach 4 north of the campground are not to be missed. The restrooms at Kalaloch were the BEST and cleanest I’ve seen in a month of travels through the park system.  Understand the restrooms where recently renovated.  Thank you NPS!

reviews.author: Katarina V.
reviews.text: This was our first campground during our PCH road trip, and we did tent camping at A048. This campground was nice and the campsite was pretty spacious. It wasn't the biggest site we've stayed at and we did have neighbors on both sides, but we still had room to move around quite a bit and it was blocked by enough vegetation to provide some privacy. We booked around 2 months in advance and really wished we could have had a beach view, but the website would not let us reserve those spots for some reason. However, we had a lot of beautiful tree coverage, which was nice because it was still in Washington's rainy season. We loved that it was right next to the beach and not far from a lot of places we wanted to go to (i.e. Tree of Life, Ruby Beach, Hoh Rainforest, Big Cedar Tree, etc.). The people were polite, the bathrooms were clean, and they had a pump with drinking water at the beginning of the loop. I thought this location had showers, but we were not able to locate them (we didn't look very hard because we got in late and left early). I wish we could have had more time here.

reviews.author: Blair d.
reviews.text: The Kalaloch Campground is ideally situated on the Washington Coast with easy access to the Hoh Rain Forest, Lake Quinalt and the most stunning beaches. The campground has potable water, restrooms, and firepits. Unfortunately, most of the campsites are built for cars with big cement slabs and the firepits are placed without thought for where a tent should go. We had a campsite along the edge of the water but no view due to lots of shrubs, and we had to push our tent into the bushes to get it set up. There are only a handful of sites that really work well for tents and only a couple of them with views. Getting a reservation here is almost impossible and after 3 years of trying it was a bit of a disappointment.

reviews.author: Gary D.
reviews.text:
Kalaloch has been my favorite place to camp since I first encountered it 56 years ago.  Lots of years tenting and many more trailering.  
The beach is miles long with no vehicles, huge driftwood logs, clean sand.  At low tide you can explore tide pools around huge rocks that are submerged at high to medium tides.  Eagles are seen multiple time a day, and this trip we saw three gray whales cavorting near the shore one morning.
Every site has a campfire ring and several have spectacular ocean views.  There were at least as many tents as RV's this trip.  
Kalaloch is about 40 miles from the fascinating moss-covered Hoh Rain Forest and 70 miles from beautiful Lake Crescent.  35 miles the other direction is Lake Quinault.  Kalaloch, Lake Crescent and Lake Quinault all have old-style timber lodges with rooms for rent, and each lodge has a decent sit-down restaurant.
Plan several days.  If Kalaloch isn't on your bucket list it should be.

This setting is close enough to the Hoh Rain Forest to include it in some excursions, but is whole by itself.  Will love to return--maybe even in the winter!

reviews.author: Kimberly G.
reviews.text: Camped here on August 25-27 and was located at campsite A62, A63, and A65 together with relatives. Too bad we didn't get the beach-side view. Our campsite was beside the freeway where logging trucks frequently pass by which was unfortunately loud especially at night - kept waking me up too so don't choose this site if you want peace and quiet. The campsite was shaded and had ample space for 2-3 tents. However, the only down side was that the sites are too close to each other that you can see your neighbor and their bonfire. Flush toilets and potable drinking water is available here too. Firewood is available at the nearby lodge for $8 a bundle so I suggest driving to the Queets Trading Post which is about 3-4 miles out for $5.50 a bundle. There were no mosquitoes as far as I can remember and with it being in a rainforest, it is quite a bit damp and wet. There are 2 trails in this campsite and we did a night hike on one of the trails (which was a bit scary but fun). Host is very friendly and funny too. Overall, I highly recommend this place for experience and I would definitely come back given that I am able to reserve the beach-side sites. Sunset was beautiful at the beach. Pet-friendly.

reviews.author: Jennifer  M.
reviews.text: Kalaloch has always been the most wonderful place! This visit was no exception as we had amazing weather the whole time we were there. Just a few things to note. The bathroom near the E loop is under construction. So there is one bathroom for D,E and F!  The whole week we were there, there appeared to be no urgency to get the project done. The construction crew was there only a few times for a few hours. The bathrooms were kept clean but there were no modifications made for the Pandemic ( no soap provided-they are still using the cold hand dryers??? - some parks have discontinued the use of them because of spreading the virus through air) Sometimes you had to wait in line for the bathroom:<(     The grate on our firepit was missing, the kind ranger said  they had some, and the only maintenance man on staff would try to find the time to bring it to us. the week went by and it never arrived. Not sure if these issues are federal funding problems or what? All that said, Kalaloch is a magical place -our family has been every summer for decades :)

reviews.author: Malisa  A.
reviews.text: The location was perfect, loved hearing the sound of the waves all night. The sites were clean and nicely spaced. It was a wonderful experience for me and my family.

reviews.author: Kerry B.
reviews.text:
I have been camping at Kalaloch my whole life and this year has been on of the worst years!  Between the Rangers and camp hosts patrolling the campground for violations and not maintaining the campground it’s not a the great place it used to be!
The website never mentioned that the bathroom by E loop was being remodeled (the whole week were there not on person was working on it.) This was my childhood favorite place and the last few years it hasn’t even remotely been the same.  The Park Rangers need to go back to educating and being their for people not jus Law Enforcement!!

reviews.author: Crystal M.
reviews.text: We had a wonderful time! We will definitely be back again someday.

reviews.author: Corrinne H.
reviews.text: We had a private site with a view of the water. It was a short walk to the beach and our boys loved playing in the wooded area. Sites along the road looked less desirable.

reviews.author: Lisa M.
reviews.text: The Kalaloch Campground was a magical and enchanting experience. The mossy trees and misty beach created the perfect setting for our first time to Olympic National Park.  We had a secluded site that had perfect trees for our hammocks.  I was so happy that the campground opened in time for us to fulfill the reservation we made six months ago.

reviews.author: Vanluk T.
reviews.text: Love it ❤️

reviews.author: Amy B.
reviews.text: Great location, love the lodge down the street! Limited cell service, gross bathrooms (how is there no soap - especially in these times?), and very busy in the summer. Sites are nice though and the beach is wonderful!

reviews.author: Chris K.
reviews.text: Nice beach and well maintained campground.  I wish they had showers.

reviews.author: Andrea E.
reviews.text: Clean restrooms..nice campsites

reviews.author: David  O.
reviews.text: I wish there would have been soap or sanitizer in the restrooms.

reviews.author: John E.
reviews.text: My kids and I camp at Kalaloch every year for the past 7 years and it has become our favorite over the years. In 2019 we camped and had a great time up until the camp host started yelling at my kids. We have never had a complaint ever and felt he could have handled things more maturely.  2020 was an amazing time and the host was polite this time. This year I made reservations nearest the bathroom as a convenience to the kids as they seem to go a lot. There was no noticed on the site or on Rec.gov of the bathroom being remodeled.  So it was a constant long journey to escort my youngest child. Also the Kalaloch market always has polite and helpful staff .Other than that issue the smell of the ocean and the crash of the waves always keeps me at peace. I definitely recommend this place.

reviews.author: Steven T.
reviews.text: Beautiful views of Pacific! Close to Hoh Rain Forest. Best for tents and small RV or travel trailers. Trailer pads are very short. Definitely recommend!!

reviews.author: Richard B.
reviews.text: Great ocean view site, close to beach walking trail and restrooms

reviews.author: Dave D.
reviews.text: Kalaloch is the mainstay campground on Olympic Pennisula. Conveniently located to popular beach accessess, and Olympic Park Destinations, and for those wanting to stay put it's own beach frontage offers relaxation, and mind cleansing stroles along the beach.

reviews.author: Lance S.
reviews.text: Kalaloch is my favorite campsite in all of Washington.  Sure, it's not as fancy as a lot of campgrounds, but the location can't be beat.

reviews.author: Keegan R.
reviews.text: Great place to camp! It was quiet, clean, and excellently located if you want to explore all the beaches nearby. Our site was great, too! It was in the perfect location where we were adequately blocked by trees and bushes so you couldn't see other campsites as much. We were so close to the bathrooms and the beach, both! We did notice that not all the sites were like this and some were either right next to each other or were easily visible through the trees. I wouldn't put much stock in trying to get beach view sites. They were teeny!

reviews.author: Chris V.
reviews.text: Got a great spot. Was a bit windy and cold but was very good weather. Only complaint I have and it's very minor is that the bathroom closest to our spot was closed for updates. It was a bit of a walk to the next one so don't wait until it's urgent. Happy they opened in time for our reservation.

reviews.author: Jen C.
reviews.text: We really enjoyed our stay at Kalaloch Campground! The campground itself is beautiful, with sites nestled beneath mature coastal trees. You can hear the waves of the ocean crashing from your tent and some sites even have an ocean view. Either way, the walk down to the beach is short - five or ten minutes from most of the campground. Here, you're only about an hour from some of the other favorite beaches of ONP (Mora Area) and the Hoh Rainforest. I highly recommend Kalaloch as a home base for this region of the park.

reviews.author: Elizabeth V.

reviews.author: Nicholas Z.
reviews.text:
While I understand that the campground just opened, I feel there was enough time to prepare the restrooms with soap and/or hand sanitizer dispensers, as well as paper towels. Also, I don’t understand why NP campgrounds inside the parks don’t all provide coin operated shower facilities! We had to go to National Forest campground in the area to shower. We are visiting many NP’s this summer- some have great restroom /shower facilities within the park and others don’t. This needs to be a priority in the future.  
As for the campground itself, I love the location and the sites themselves! Enjoyed the Park immensely!

reviews.text: We always enjoy our stay at Kalaloch, BUT a lot of times we cannot reserve a space on line. We are not particular in which space we stay in, we have been going there for about 20+ years and do have some favorite spaces and not always with a water view which are nice sometimes but we are flexible.
