reviews.author: Carrie K.
reviews.text: We stayed at Kalaloch August 18 and 19th. I looked for date options in June and those were the only 2 consecutive nights fir the summer I could find! Reserve early!  Our site was in an inner loop and had decent privacy for its location. We were not far from the bathroom, dish wash station, and beach stairs. We lucked out for sure. The campground was full, but didnt seem crowded or loud. There is tons of space on the beach to spread out, so again you dont feel crowded. We visited a few other beaches, walked to the Ranger station (easy walk a little bit is on the edge of the road), and did our Junior Rangers. We have already reserved our space for summer of 2020!

reviews.author: Aidan O.
reviews.text:
Kalaloch campground is nice and well-maintained. Scenery is spectacular, with trees shaped by wind and a massive sandy beach. Make sure to check out the Tree of Life below the campground - it looks dramatically different depending on the time of day, if skies are clear and sunny.  

That's kinda the crux of it, though. It's not always clear and sunny, as it rains a lot at Kalaloch. I'm sure you know that and are checking the forecast, but in my experience the sites take on a lot of water and don't drain it very well. We had fun engineering a set of drainage ditches but this campground can get pretty dreary when wet. 

The sites are also often very close together, I assume due to the park's summer popularity. There are several loops that are more private (they're pretty clear on the map) but in general I wouldn't count on much privacy unless you're here in the off season. In short, Kalaloch is a really, really nice beach and it has a really nice campground - there's just better campgrounds out there. I'd still highly recommend this to anyone for a sunny weekend or longer.

reviews.author: Valerie  P.

reviews.text: We camped in a tent and the tent site was all tucked deep into the woods which made us feel like we were all alone! I love that the beach is left unkept and you have to climb over huge logs to get there. We had a spot that looked really far from the beach on the map, but in reality, it was less than a minute walk! It is a far drive from the rest of the park which is quite spread out anyway. So be prepared to wake up early to get where you're going.

reviews.text: Good memories

reviews.author: Paul S.
reviews.text: Needs showers, that would be an incredible enhancement, please do not increase senior pass fees, please do not PRIVATIZE any of our National parks.   I love Kaaloch and the Olympic NP.

reviews.author: Meng W.
reviews.text: Drive is gorgeous and full of places to stop once you get into the park. The sunlight drifting through the mossy trees makes it look like a fairytale...it's really something else. I recommend exploring as much of the coast as you can - lots of trails with aforementioned fairytale feelz. The whole place felt private and so expansive as the camping spots were limited. We booked it last minute and didn't get a spot near the beach but it was practically there - just a 1 minute walk, all of the spots will work fine but of course if you can get a spot with a view of the ocean do it. Everyone at the camp was friendly and laid back, just there to enjoy nature. We had a picnic on the beach watching the unreal sunset. Will for sure be doing this every single year as much as I can. This is why we need to protect our forests. Thank you to those who keep it thriving and pristine.

reviews.author: Christiane  M.
reviews.text: Site is beautiful, calm. The campground host was very friendly and helpful, we had not very much experience with our hired RV, but he managed it all. Thank so much. If the Pacific Coast would be not so far away from Germany, we would come every year.

reviews.author: Rebecca P.
reviews.text: Beautiful location for single family camping. Great ocean view.

reviews.author: Guillaume C.
reviews.text: Exceptional site.  Restrooms could use some TLC.

reviews.author: Michael N.
reviews.text: Your most important decision will be to book early and as close to the ocean side cliffs as possible. If you leave it up to chance you'll most likely be assigned a campsite adjacent to highway 1. Oh joy! Not so annoying during the day with normal activities about. But when night falls and especially in the early AM you'll be bombarded be the random very loud trucks driving by. So if you're a light sleeper be very aware of this. Otherwise it is a truly beautiful site where the boreal rainforest  meets the Pacific ocean. Expect rain, hence the designation of rainforest.
